info.title: WideCast.ai Public API
info.summary: Turn plain-text scripts into AI-generated short-form videos.
info.description:
WideCast.ai turns plain-text scripts (and soon ideas, audio, existing videos)
into AI-generated short-form videos: scenes + voice + B-roll, ready for
review in the scene editor.

## ⚠ AGENT PRE-FLIGHT RULES (read once when you import this spec)

Two skills define the FULL scope of WideCast workflows. **Load the relevant
one BEFORE any other endpoint call** — they are key-free, idempotent, and
cheap (~1 call). Skipping them is the single most common cause of
weak/incomplete output.

1. **Edit/audit an EXISTING video.** When the user gives a WideCast
   scene-editor URL (`record2.html#scene_editor?topic_id=…` on
   widecast.ai) OR a `topic_id` (looks like `widecast…` / `gubo…` /
   current id) AND signals an editing intent ("edit this video", "refine
   the scenes", "fix scene N", "review/audit the video", "improve
   overlay", "fix thumbnail", "audit backgrounds", "redo scene",
   "biên tập video", "chỉnh sửa cảnh", "sửa scene", "编辑视频",
   "剪辑", "シーン編集", "ビデオ編集") — **call `GET /v1/skills/editing`
   FIRST before any other endpoint**, including before `/v1/video_data`.
   Do NOT ask the user what to edit — the skill defines scope = full
   audit + fix. After the response arrives, follow its instructions
   (currently a 4-step download + Read flow that loads SKILL.md from
   disk).

2. **Author a NEW video / blog / social caption.** When the user wants
   a new piece ("make a video", "write a script", "turn this into a
   video", "write a blog", "viết bài", "做视频", etc.) — call
   `GET /v1/skills/writing?format=video` (or `blog` / `social`) FIRST.
   The skill returns a 5-step method + the full method markdown.

3. Every response from `/v1/video_data`, `/v1/scene_geometry`,
   `/v1/scene_inspector`, `/v1/modify_scene` carries a `skill_required`
   field as a backup signal — if you see it, you have not loaded the
   skill yet and should do so before continuing.

4. When in doubt about intent, prefer loading the skill (cheap) over
   asking the user (slow + breaks autonomous-run contract).

## Authentication

Every request needs an API key, passed as
`Authorization: Bearer wc_live_*`. Generate keys in the dashboard
(Setup Center → API Keys). Each call to `/v1/create_video` consumes
credits from your account; usage (calls + credits) is tracked per key.
**Exception**: `/v1/skills/writing`, `/v1/skills/editing`, `/v1/status/{id}`,
`/v1/solo/pubkey`, `/v1/agent/signup/start` and `/v1/agent/signup/verify` are key-free.
An AI agent with no key gets one from the owner's email: `startAgentSignup` emails a 6-digit
code, `verifyAgentSignup` turns the code the owner reads back into the account's key. Store
that key at once and never show it in chat; the only thing the owner reads or types is the code.

## Two input flows (`source`) × two completion gates (`output_type`)

### `source` — what kind of input you provide

1. **`source: "text"`** (default) — you provide `script_text` (80-500
   words), used VERBATIM by the narrator. No AI rewriting.
2. **`source: "idea"`** — you provide `idea_text` (5-1000 words, longer
   gets auto-truncated). The server writes a narration from the idea
   (AI), then continues the same scene-sourcing flow as `text`. You
   also pick `language`, `video_length` (short/normal), and
   `research_enabled`.
3. **`source: "blog"`** — you provide `blog_text` (30-3000 words — an
   article to repurpose; longer auto-truncated). Identical pipeline to
   `idea` (same AI script-writer), just a longer input. Same optional
   `language` / `video_length` / `research_enabled`.

`idea` and `blog` are **generative sources**: the server writes the script
first (Phase 1), so they support `output_type: "text"` to stop at the
editable script. Future generative sources (audio, video) follow the
same shape.

### `output_type` — how far down the pipeline to run (pipeline depth)

1. **`output_type: "text"`** — stop after the source→script-text phase.
   Returns a `review_url` (the UI auto-detects the data is narration-only
   and opens the Script Editor). **Only valid for generative sources**
   (`source != "text"`) — for `source: "text"` you already supplied the
   script, so `text` output would echo your input (HTTP 400).
2. **`output_type: "scene"`** (default) — stop at "scenes ready for
   review". You get back a `review_url` to inspect / edit before deciding
   to render the final MP4. Optional follow-up: `POST /v1/export_video`.
3. **`output_type: "video"`** — run end-to-end without manual review.
   `result.video_url` populated when the final MP4 is ready. Use this
   when you trust the generated scenes (programmatic / batch use).

The two axes combine — every valid `source` × `output_type` pair works,
except `source: "text"` + `output_type: "text"` (rejected — see above).

## Endpoints

- **POST `/v1/create_video`** — submit `script_text`/`idea_text` + optional
  `output_type`. Returns a `widecast*` id and initial `status: "processing"`.
- **POST `/v1/export_video`** — for `output_type: "scene"` videos that
  reached `scenes_ready_for_review`, kick the final-MP4 renderer.
  Idempotent — calling twice is a no-op.
- **GET `/v1/status/{id}`** — poll until `status` is `completed` (or
  `failed`). `result.review_url` is present from the first response
  (`pending`/`processing` too) — it's a stable id-keyed page, so you can
  show it to the user immediately. The completion gate depends on the
  video's `output_type`:
    * text  → `stage: "script_ready_for_review"`.
    * scene → `stage: "scenes_ready_for_review"`.
    * video → `stage: "video_rendered"`, `result.video_url` also set.

Polling cadence: start at 5s, exponential backoff (×1.5) up to 60s. The
SDKs implement this automatically via `video.wait()`.

## Script bounds (LOCKED)

`script_text` is used **verbatim** by the narrator — no rewriting. The
bounds reflect what fits inside a short-form video:

- **Minimum 80 words** (~20s of narration) — anything shorter renders
  a useless clip.
- **Maximum 500 words** (~120s / 2 min of narration) — beyond this,
  render cost and pacing both suffer.

## Inline media in `script_text`

Drop a **direct image or video URL** into the script next to the line it
should illustrate — WideCast strips it from the narration and uses it as
that scene's visual instead of auto-sourced B-roll. Two equivalent forms:

* **Markdown image syntax** (recommended for AI-chat callers):
  `![brief scene description](https://cdn.acme.com/coldbrew.jpg)`. Chat
  hosts (Claude / ChatGPT / Grok / Gemini) render the picture inline so
  the user can SEE whether the visual fits the narration before
  approving the script. The alt text doubles as the strongest possible
  scene anchor.
* **Raw URL** on its own line (works the same; backward-compatible):
  `Our cold brew steeps for 16 hours. https://cdn.acme.com/coldbrew.jpg
  That mellow finish is what people come back for.`

Direct file links only (image `.png/.jpg/.jpeg/.gif/.webp/.bmp/.avif/.svg`,
video `.mp4/.webm/.mov/.m4v/.avi`); page links like a YouTube watch URL
are not inlined (use `source="video_url"` for those). See the
`script_text` field for details.

## Field-requirement convention (LOCKED)

Every constraint on every field — validation bounds, enum values,
required-vs-optional, defaults — appears in **four places**, kept in
sync:

1. **OpenAPI spec** — `description`, `minimum`/`maximum`, `enum`,
   `default`. Single source devs read first.
2. **SDK constants + types** — named exports in `widecast` (Python) and
   `@widecast/sdk` (TypeScript), so callers can refer to them
   programmatically without re-typing the literal.
3. **Markdown docs** — `Field reference` table in each endpoint page.
4. **Server enforcement** — rejected requests must surface a LOCKED
   `error.code` (e.g. `script_too_short`, `invalid_output_type`).

The SDK parity test (`test_script_bounds_constants_locked` and
equivalents) imports each SDK constant and asserts the exact numeric
value — changing one surface without the others breaks the test. New
endpoints MUST follow this same pattern.

## Conventions (locked — changing = breaking)

- Snake_case JSON fields
- **ID format**: `widecast<alphanumeric>` (~20 chars). The server's new-script
  detection checks for the literal `"widecast"` substring, so SDKs/clients MUST
  not strip it. Public id == internal `topic_id` (1:1, no mapping).
- API key prefixes: `wc_live_*`
- Object marker: every resource has `"object": "<type>"`
- Status enum: `pending | processing | completed | failed`
  (`pending` ONLY covers the brief race window between create + worker
  writing the topic row; once the row exists, status is `processing` —
  the abroll worker doesn't increment `step` until the end)
- Error envelope: `{ "error": { "type", "code", "message", "param?",
  "doc_url", "request_id" } }`
- Error codes (v0.1.0): `account_expired | credit_exhausted |
  render_failed | unknown_error | scenes_not_ready | export_failed |
  script_too_short | script_too_long | invalid_output_type |
  invalid_source | idea_too_short | missing_idea_text |
  blog_too_short | missing_blog_text |
  missing_video_url | missing_audio_url | missing_media_file |
  unsupported_media_url | media_too_long | file_too_large |
  missing_api_key | invalid_api_key |
  invalid_language | invalid_video_length | invalid_research_enabled |
  invalid_faceless | invalid_production_mode | invalid_presenter | presenter_not_ready | plan_required |
  invalid_purpose | invalid_adjust | invalid_content_type | invalid_intervention_level |
  ideas_failed | invalid_publish_input | invalid_platforms |
  no_platforms_connected | publish_not_ready | download_failed |
  publish_failed | free_tier_limit_exceeded | telegram_not_connected |
  telegram_send_failed | invalid_parse_mode | conflicting_media |
  invalid_photo_url | invalid_video_url | message_too_long |
  rate_limited | scenes_not_ready | invalid_script | invalid_by |
  invalid_field_entry | scene_not_found | unsupported_field |
  object_level_edit_disabled | remotion_spec_disabled |
  remotion_spec_not_found | remotion_spec_parse_failed |
  remotion_spec_invalid | missing_remotion_object_rect |
  invalid_remotion_add_element | invalid_remotion_add_element_kind |
  invalid_text_edit | missing_text_edit | no_svg_overlay_source |
  invalid_disable_overlay_value | invalid_module_id | module_not_found |
  skill_unavailable |
  missing_uploaded_overlay_url | invalid_uploaded_overlay_url |
  svg2spec_failed |
  missing_voice_file | mixed_remotion_fields | ambiguous_text |
  invalid_media_url | modify_failed | persist_failed |
  voice_upload_queue_failed | narrator_video_upload_queue_failed |

  unsupported_action |
  publisher_missing | mqtt_publish_failed | no_live_editor |
  no_active_editor | browser_error |
  screenshot_publish_failed | server_fallback_failed |
  invalid_scripts | invalid_recommended_format | topic_exists |
  script_seed_failed`
- Headers (every response): `X-Request-Id`, `X-RateLimit-*`,
  `X-WideCast-Version`
- Timestamps: ISO 8601 UTC strings (e.g. `2026-05-19T17:30:00Z`)
- Pagination (future): cursor-based — see `ListEnvelope` schema

post.description:
Create a video from either a plain-text script (`source: "text"`) or
a short idea description (`source: "idea"`). The server wraps the
same background workers that power the Script Editor + Idea-to-Video
flows in the WideCast UI.

- Returns immediately with `status: "processing"` (HTTP 202). Poll
  `GET /v1/status/{id}` until terminal.
- If `wait_for_render: true`, blocks up to **60 seconds**. If render
  completes within the window, returns `status: "completed"` (HTTP 200).
  Otherwise returns the in-flight state and the client polls.

### source

- `"text"` (default — backward-compat): provide `script_text`
  (80-500 words, used VERBATIM by the narrator). Worker:
  `request_video_script_from_script`.
- `"idea"`: provide `idea_text` (5-1000 words; >1000 auto-truncated)
  plus optional `language` / `video_length` / `research_enabled`.
  Worker chain: `ai_enhance_script` (idea → narration) →
  `request_video_script_from_script` (narration → scenes).

### output_type

- `"scene"` (default): pipeline stops at scenes-ready-for-review.
  `result.review_url` is in the create response itself (safe to share
  immediately — the page handles early arrival). You can then call
  `POST /v1/export_video` to render the final MP4.
- `"video"`: pipeline auto-chains into the renderer once scenes are
  ready. `result.review_url` ships from the create response; the
  `result.video_url` field appears on completion. No manual
  `/v1/export_video` call needed.

### Agent guidance — open `review_url` inline if you can

When you surface `result.review_url` to the user, **also open it in
your built-in web viewer if your runtime exposes one** (Codex
view-url, ChatGPT browse tool, any host that can iframe an external
URL, future inline browsers). The review page is a full scene
editor — letting the user inspect / swap / approve scenes inside
the same chat is dramatically better UX than asking them to
copy-paste a link into another tab. If you have no such tool, just
show the URL as a clickable link.

### Bounds (LOCKED — see SDK constants)

| Field | When required | Min words | Max words | Over-max behavior |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `script_text` | source=text | 80 (`SCRIPT_MIN_WORDS`) | 500 (`SCRIPT_MAX_WORDS`) | reject `script_too_long` |
| `idea_text` | source=idea | 5 (`IDEA_MIN_WORDS`) | 1000 (`IDEA_MAX_WORDS`) | auto-truncate, surfaced in `details.input_truncated_from` |
| `blog_text` | source=blog | 30 (`BLOG_MIN_WORDS`) | 3000 (`BLOG_MAX_WORDS`) | auto-truncate, surfaced in `details.input_truncated_from` |

SDKs export these as named constants — refer to those instead of
hard-coding the numbers. Word count = whitespace split, works for
English + Vietnamese.

post.summary: Kick the final-MP4 renderer for an already-created video.
post.description:
Pairs with `output_type: "scene"` on `/v1/create_video`. After the
scenes-ready callback (or manual review via `review_url`), call this
to enqueue the final render.

Idempotent — calling twice is a no-op. Returns the current
`/v1/status` snapshot.

Preconditions:
- The video must have reached `scenes_ready_for_review` (HTTP 409 with
  `error.code = "scenes_not_ready"` otherwise).

Post-effects:
- The video's effective `output_type` is promoted to `"video"`.
- The completion gate becomes `result.video_url` non-empty.
- The `video.completed` webhook (if `callback_url` is set) re-arms
  and fires when the MP4 is rendered.

post.summary: Open/close the per-video edit session for an AI editing run.
post.description:
Synchronous, free. Manages a per-video in-memory edit session that
makes an AI editing run **safe under parallel scene edits** and
gives **instant read-after-write**.

- `action="start"` — before the first scene edit: the server caches
  the whole video document in memory. Every `/v1/modify_scene`
  write lands in the cache (crash-safe via a write-ahead file),
  every read (`/v1/video_data`, `/v1/scene_geometry`,
  `/v1/scene_inspector`) is served fresh from the cache, and
  ElasticSearch is written ONCE at commit. This eliminates version
  conflicts across parallel scene-editor subagents.
- `action="commit"` — after the last scene: flushes the cache to
  permanent storage. **Required to finish a run** (an idle session
  auto-commits after 45 minutes / 2700 s as a backstop).
- `action="abort"` — discards staged edits without writing.
- `action="status"` — reports `{active, staged_writes}`.

If the response has `cache_enabled=false` the server is in legacy
direct-write mode — proceed WITHOUT a session; writes are still
serialized per video by the server-side lock.

id.description: topic_id of the video being edited. `topic_id` accepted as an alias.

200.description:
Edit-session state. Fields vary by `action` — `ttl_seconds` on
start, `committed` on commit, `aborted` on abort,
`staged_writes`/`started`/`last_write` on status.

cache_enabled.description: false → legacy direct-write mode; proceed without a session.

staged_writes.description: Set on action=status — pending cached writes.

ttl_seconds.description: Set on action=start — idle auto-commit backstop (2700).

400.description: `invalid_id` (missing/malformed topic_id) or `invalid_action` (not start/commit/abort/status).

404.description: `topic_not_found` — no video with this id (action=start).

502.description: `topic_fetch_failed` — could not load the video document to start a session.

post.summary: Edit ONE scene (media / overlay / layout / audio / text / metadata). Free.
post.description:
Synchronous for most branches (some upload branches are async — see
below), **no credit charged** until `/v1/export_video` re-renders
the final MP4. Successful edits publish MQTT realtime to every open
scene editor so the user sees the change live.

**Agent rule — data-first**. Call `/v1/video_data` first and use
`voice_file` (the stable per-scene UID, also the base of
`{voice_file}_spec.json`) for `by`/`value`. For **layout edits**,
also call `/v1/scene_geometry` to read narrator/caption/Remotion
object boxes in 280×498 editor-preview coords without ever
rendering a screenshot. `segment.id` is only display/order metadata
and may change after reorder/add/delete.

Resolves the target scene with `by` + `value`:
  - `by="voice_file"` — exact match on the stable per-scene UID
    (preferred).
  - `by="id"` — exact match on the current `segment.id` order/display.
  - `by="text"` — fuzzy match against `segment.text`. Multi-match →
    HTTP 200 `ClarificationResponse` — ask the user to pick a
    `voice_file`, then re-call.

**Pick exactly ONE field family per call.** The only intentional
multi-family call is `layout.batch`, which composes layout-only
children (`overlay.narrator.*`, `overlay.caption.y`,
`remotion.object.rect`, `remotion.group.rect`).

**(A) Background media swap (`mediaUrl` / `mediaType`).** Roll-
aware: B-roll scene → asset IS the background (`mediaUrl`,
`brollUrl`, `thumbnailUrl`, `brollThumbnailUrl` synced); A-roll
scene → narrator and grid untouched, asset registered as
`user_asset_url` / `brollUrl`.

**(B) Upload Overlay (`remotion.upload_overlay`).** Free, agent-
supplied asset → Remotion spec (not Regenerate Overlay, which is
paid). **Two upload formats, chosen by URL extension**:

  - **📐 SVG path (PREFERRED for agent-authored overlays)** —
    URL ends `.svg` (case-insensitive). WideCast routes through
    `svg2spec`: parses the SVG, finds every
    `<g data-wc-object="name">` group, rasterizes EACH group
    ALONE on a transparent 720×1280 canvas, crops to the alpha
    bbox, and emits one Storyboard object per group with
    **pixel-perfect placement (NO auto-fit; max diff 2/255 vs
    original)**. **Required**: viewBox `0 0 720 1280` (portrait).
    Per-group attributes:

      * `data-wc-object="name"` — REQUIRED stable id/name;
        groups without it are rasterized as background.
      * `data-wc-kind` ∈ {`object`, `text`, `bar`, `mark`,
        `callout`} — inferred if missing.
      * `data-wc-anim` ∈ {`slide-up`, `slide-down`,
        `slide-left`, `slide-right`, `pop`, `grow-x`, `grow-y`,
        `fade`, …} — default `fade`; bar shapes get
        `growRight`/`growUp` automatically.
      * `data-wc-z` — paint/stack order; default = document
        order.

    Use the SVG path when you want **deterministic
    decomposition** (no classifier in the loop) plus explicit
    animation hints in one authored file. SVG-specific errors:
    HTTP 422 `svg2spec_failed` (parse / viewBox / structure
    errors with detail message), HTTP 502 (SVG download failed).

  - **🖼 Raster path (default)** — URL extension is PNG / JPG /
    WebP / GIF / etc. Pipeline classifies the uploaded image as
    `graphic` vs `realistic`, decomposes graphic images into
    objects, and falls back to a full-frame single-image overlay
    for realistic ones (strict no-AI fallback — no Nano Banana,
    no image generation). For best object-decomposed raster
    specs: portrait 9:16 transparent PNG (720×1280 preferred) or
    flat-bg graphic with large separated foreground objects/text,
    strong contrast, readable typography; avoid photo-realistic
    backgrounds, heavy gradients, vignettes, tiny dense text.

Whichever format you use, ground the asset in scene context
(`text`, `talking_point`, `visual`, `quote`, `keyword`, `type`).
Explicit opt-in to recreate an overlay even when
`remotion_spec="none"`. Response includes a cache-busted
`remotion_spec_url` and `remotion_poster_url` (server-side
inspector fallback poster).

**(C) Remotion Storyboard object-layer rect
(`remotion.object.rect`) — PREFERRED overlay layout API.** First
call `/v1/scene_geometry` and read
`boxes.remotion.object_layer.objects`; each item has `layout_id`
(e.g. `main.one_by_one`, `main.obj_03_text`), `rect` (280×498
preview), `rect_canvas` (720×1280), temporal policy, and the
update field name. Then send
`{field_name: "remotion.object.rect", value: {layout_id, x?, y?,
w?, h?, coordinate_space: "preview"|"canvas"}}` (one or more
entries). The agent edits simple visible object boxes; WideCast
maps the rect back to raw Storyboard object offsets/sizes and
keeps the group wrapper unchanged. For `one_by_one`, scene_geometry
exposes ONE logical `*.one_by_one` rect — editing it transforms
all timed sequence items together. Object-layer x/y may produce
negative raw offsets relative to the group; allowed and matches
Remotion rendering. Spec-changing edits refresh
`{voice_file}_overlay_poster.png` used by server-side scene
inspector fallback.

**(D) Remotion Storyboard group rect (`remotion.group.rect`) —
low-level wrapper edit; prefer (C) for visible overlay layout.**
`value = {element_id?, x?, y?, w?, h?, coordinate_space:
"canvas"|"preview", resize_mode?:
"scale_children"|"wrapper_only"}`. Move-only (x/y) updates the
group wrapper; child objects untouched. Group x/y are NOT clamped
— `y:-120` legitimately translates a full-canvas group upward.
Resize (w/h) defaults to `scale_children` (wrapper + every child +
root `background.bbox` scale together). `wrapper_only` is advanced.

**(E) Narrator layout rect (`overlay.narrator.rect`).** Legacy
**280×498 editor preview** coords. Either send
`{x, y, w, h, visible?, animation?, borderRadius?}` or field-by-
field via `overlay.narrator.x | y | w | h`. Preserves existing
narrator metadata and source-space `segment.narrator_face` (do
NOT mutate `narrator_face` for layout edits — `scene_geometry`
converts it through the current narrator rect for display).
Marks `overlay.narrator.touched=true` so auto-fit doesn't
overwrite. No media / audio / timeline / Remotion spec changes.

**(F) Caption Y layout (`overlay.caption.y`).** 280×498 preview
coords. Updates ONLY `overlay.caption.y` plus `touched=true`. Does
NOT edit x/w/h, visibility, config/style, `segment.text`,
`segment.words`, audio, duration, or Remotion specs.

**(G) Layout batch (`layout.batch`) — one persist, one MQTT.**
Either send multiple layout fields directly OR wrap as
`{field_name: "layout.batch", value: {fields: [...]}}`. WideCast
persists `generated_video_script` ONCE and broadcasts ONE
`scene_modified` MQTT event after all children succeed. Allowed
children: `overlay.narrator.*`, `overlay.caption.y`,
`remotion.object.rect`, `remotion.group.rect`. DISALLOWED:
`mediaUrl`/`mediaType`, `voice.upload`, `narrator.upload_video`,
`remotion.upload_overlay`, `roll.active`/`roll.switch`,
`segment.text`, metadata fields.

**(H) Upload Voice (`voice.upload`) — async.** User-supplied
audio (not Use-AI-Voice). Returns
`{object: "scene_voice_upload_queued", queue_id:
"gs_{topic_id}_{voice_file}", status: "queued"}`. On completion
the server applies `words` / `text` / `duration` / following-
scene shifts / caption timelines / `narrator_face` / `recorded`
flags to `generated_video_script` and emits MQTT
`event="scene_voice_upload_applied"`. Verify with
`/v1/video_data` after.

**(I) Upload Narrator Video (`narrator.upload_video`) — async.**
User-supplied A-roll video. If target is B-roll, the server
preserves the previous background in
`brollUrl`/`brollThumbnailUrl` and applies the same roll-switch
helper as `roll.active="A"` on completion. Returns
`{object: "scene_narrator_upload_queued", queue_id, status:
"queued"}`; completion emits MQTT
`event="scene_narrator_upload_applied"`.

**(J) A/B-roll switch (`roll.active` / `roll.switch`) — sync data
switch.** Preserves both lanes (`arollUrl`/`brollUrl`) and swaps
active runtime fields (`mediaUrl`, `thumbnailUrl`, `mediaType`,
`active_roll`, `show_narrator`, audio flags, `recorded`,
`videoTrim`). On A→B mirrors the UI's `_switched` file-family
protection when files exist. No upload / transcode / generate.

**(K) Segment text correction (`segment.text`) — sync.** Updates
`segment.text`, rebuilds `segment.words` over existing audio
timings, syncs the current caption-language entry. Does NOT
change audio, duration, or following-scene timelines.

**(L) Scene metadata** — pick from this family only: `pattern`,
`visual`, `keyword`, `quote`, `talking_point`, `type`, `sub_mode`
(or `segment.<name>` / `scene.<name>` forms). `pattern` is
validated against ai_segment_text canonical values; `type` ∈
{HOOK, STAT, KEY POINT, DATA, FACT, CALL TO ACTION};
`pattern="illustration"` requires `sub_mode` ∈
{photo_with_people, photo_no_people, document, digital_ui}.
`pattern="narration_only"` auto-clears quote+visual;
`pattern="typography_only"` auto-clears visual.

**(M) Remotion add element (`remotion.add_element`) — FREE,
SYNC, ADD-ONLY**. Append a new Storyboard group/object to the
existing spec. `value = {kind, value?, label?, url?, position?,
rect?, style_token?, emphasis?}` — OR a bare string for
`kind="text"`. `kind` ∈ {`text`, `stat`, `label`, `callout`,
`image`} (aliases: `metric`/`number`→`stat`,
`badge`/`caption`→`label`; defaults to `image` when `url` /
`image` / `src` set, else `text`). Optional placement hint
`position` ∈ {top, bottom, left, right, center} for the
server-picked default rect; OR pin a rect explicitly via
`rect: {x, y, w, h, coordinate_space: "preview"|"canvas"}`
(default 280×498 preview). Optional `entry` (default `fade`),
`delay_sec`, `z_index`, `element_z_index` (default 900). The
branch **does NOT auto-fit, replace, move, or modify existing
objects** and **must be sent alone** (returns 400
`mixed_remotion_fields` if combined with other Remotion fields,
and is not allowed inside `layout.batch` directly). Requires an
enabled spec — returns 409 `remotion_spec_disabled` for scenes
where `segment.remotion_spec="none"`. Response `applied`
carries the new `element_id`, `object_id`, and
`layout_id` (= `{element_id}.{object_id}`, e.g.
`agent_add_01.add_text_1782700000000`) plus `rect` (preview),
`rect_canvas` (720×1280), `auto_fit: false`,
`cost: "free_spec_append"`, plus a `follow_up` hint. **Standard
workflow**: immediately after `remotion.add_element` returns the
new `layout_id`, call `/v1/scene_geometry` to read the
displayed rect + violations, then send a `layout.batch` carrying
a `remotion.object.rect` with that `layout_id` to land the
element inside safe zones — the initial placement is a default,
not a polished layout.

**(N) Disable overlay (`disable_overlay`) — FREE, SYNC, data
edit.** `field_name = "disable_overlay"` (aliases:
`remotion.disable_overlay`, `overlay.disable`,
`remotion_spec.none`). `value` may be `true`, the string
`"none"`, or `{enabled:false}`. **What it does**: sets
`segment.remotion_spec="none"` (the opt-out sentinel) and emits
MQTT `scene_modified` with `overlay_disabled: true`. **What it
does NOT do**: it does NOT delete `{voice_file}_spec.json`, does
NOT delete `{voice_file}_overlay_poster.png`, does NOT
regenerate a replacement, and does NOT touch narrator / caption
/ media / timing / layout. Must be sent **alone** — combining
with other Remotion fields returns 400 `mixed_remotion_fields`.
Re-disabling a scene that is already `remotion_spec="none"`
returns `applied.idempotent: true`. **Re-enable** by calling
(B) Upload Overlay (`remotion.upload_overlay`) or the manual
regenerate-overlay flow — those write a fresh
`{voice_file}_spec.json` and stamp the segment's `remotion_spec`
to `{voice_file}_spec.json?v={mtime}`. Errors: 400
`invalid_disable_overlay_value` / `mixed_remotion_fields`,
409 `missing_voice_file`.

**(O) Overlay TEXT edit (`overlay.text_edit`) — FREE, SYNC,
0-LLM, SVG-sourced overlays only.** Change ONLY the words of an
existing overlay object without re-authoring or re-uploading.
`value = {wc_object: "<g data-wc-object id>", lines?: ["NEW LINE
1", "NEW LINE 2"], fill?: "#1E6091"}` (`lines` retypes the group;
`fill` is an optional hex colour that repaints the group's main
text - send `lines` and/or `fill`, a fill-only edit keeps the
existing words; one per group). The server
rewrites `{voice_file}_overlay.svg` in place (face-stack copies
update together; fewer lines delete slots, extra lines stack
below), re-rasterizes ONLY the touched groups, and patches the
existing spec objects — layout, narrator-fit shifts, and manual
positions on other objects are preserved. Requires an SVG-sourced
spec (`spec._source="svg2spec"`: endpoint posters and previously
uploaded SVG overlays); typography and image scenes return 422
`no_svg_overlay_source` (for typography, edit `quote` via (L)
scene metadata and regenerate instead). Poster copy rules (max 3
lines, max 4 words/line, uppercase) come back as
`applied.warnings` only — the typed copy is sovereign, but long
lines shrink to fit the safe band. The `type="thumbnail"` clone
of an edited opening poster is NOT auto-synced: apply the same
`overlay.text_edit` to the thumbnail scene's `voice_file`. Must
be sent **alone** (400 `mixed_remotion_fields`). Errors: 400
`invalid_text_edit` / `missing_text_edit`, 404
`remotion_spec_not_found`, 409 `remotion_spec_disabled` /
`missing_voice_file`, 422 `no_svg_overlay_source`.

**`remotion_spec="none"`**: user intentionally disabled the
overlay on that scene (via (N) Disable overlay or UI). Layout
edits return `remotion_spec_disabled`. Do NOT auto-enable —
only re-enable via (B) Upload Overlay if the user asks.

Successful edits publish MQTT realtime so open editors hot-update.
Final render cost lands when `/v1/export_video` is called again.

post.summary: Data-only scene layout geometry (cheap, no screenshot). Free.
post.description:
SYNCHRONOUS, free, read-only. **Use this after `/v1/video_data` and
before any screenshot/vision step** when an agent needs to audit
layout cheaply or pick coordinates for `/v1/modify_scene`. Resolves
the scene by stable `voice_file` (preferred), loads
`{voice_file}_spec.json` if available, and maps legacy narrator /
caption boxes plus Remotion Storyboard display boxes into one
**280×498 editor-preview** coordinate space.

Returns:
  - `coordinate_space` — `{width: 280, height: 498, unit:
    "editor_preview_px"}`.
  - `safe_zones` — `dead_top` (top 10% reserved), `dead_bottom`
    (bottom 25% reserved), `safe_rect` between them.
  - `scene` — `{text, talking_point, type, pattern, keyword,
    visual, quote, show_narrator, active_roll}`.
  - `boxes.narrator` — `{rect, visible, face_source, face,
    face_center, face_coordinate_space_note}`. `face` is the
    **displayed** face box, computed by converting source-space
    `segment.narrator_face` through the current
    `overlay.narrator.rect`. Do NOT mutate `segment.narrator_face`
    for layout edits — `narrator_face` is the source-space box for
    the narrator media and only refreshes when narrator media is
    generated/recorded/uploaded.
  - `boxes.caption` — `{container_rect, text_rect_estimate,
    visible}`. The caption box is read-only for layout decisions;
    the only mutable caption field is `overlay.caption.y` via
    `/v1/modify_scene`.
  - `boxes.remotion.object_layer.objects[]` — **the agent-facing
    layer**. Each item carries `layout_id` (e.g. `main.one_by_one`,
    `main.obj_03_text`), `rect` (280×498 preview), `rect_canvas`
    (720×1280), `temporal_policy`, and the update field name to
    pass back to `/v1/modify_scene`
    (`{field_name:"remotion.object.rect", value:{layout_id, x, y,
    w, h, coordinate_space:"preview"}}`). For `one_by_one`,
    scene_geometry exposes ONE logical `*.one_by_one` rect — the
    server transforms all timed sequence items together.
  - `boxes.remotion.groups[]` / `boxes.remotion.objects[]` /
    `boxes.remotion.sequence_objects[]` — lower-level debug data
    (STATIC/POSTER display boxes resolved with the same Storyboard
    math used by `{voice_file}_overlay_poster.png`).
  - `remotion_spec` — metadata for the loaded `{voice_file}_spec.json`
    (file, url, version, state). Internal `remotion_poster_*`
    keys are diagnostic-only — pass `include_diagnostics:true`
    to surface them.
  - `summary` — `{remotion_object_count,
    remotion_object_layer_count, remotion_sequence_object_count,
    remotion_group_count, remotion_temporal_policies,
    remotion_geometry_basis}`.

**Mechanical linter output is debug-only.** By default the
response is actionable data only — `violations[]` (collision
codes), `warnings[]` (mobile-readability / face-staleness hints),
and `summary.error_count` / `summary.warning_count` are
stripped. Vision-capable agents should judge collisions and
aesthetics from a screenshot via `/v1/scene_inspector`; LLM-only
agents should still proceed with the rects + `boxes.narrator.face`
to keep overlays off the face. Pass `include_diagnostics: true`
to opt back in for server/debug audits.

Designed for LLM-only agents that cannot see images: reason over
JSON, then call `/v1/modify_scene` with a `layout.batch` containing
`overlay.narrator.rect`, `overlay.caption.y`,
`remotion.object.rect` — or single-field calls. Never broadcasts
MQTT, never renders screenshots, never exposes base64 assets, and
never modifies the video.

post.summary: Upload an audio / video / image / document (or mint a pre-signed S3 PUT URL).
post.description:
Get an asset into WideCast's `widecast-assets` S3 bucket and back
out as a **public URL** the AI agent can feed into `/v1/create_video`
(as `audio_url` or `video_url`), paste into `script_text` as an
inline `![alt](url)` for images, OR `curl <get_url>` to fetch a
document body before passing it as `blog_text` / `script_text`.
This is the **canonical upload path** for AI agents handling
user-attached files — it removes the need to shop for third-party
hosts (transfer.sh / catbox / S3 of your own) or inline-base64
binary content into create_video.

**Lifecycle: the bucket prefix `assets/` auto-deletes after 24
hours.** Call `/v1/create_video` with the returned URL within that
window. Free (no credits).

**Allowed kinds**:
  * Media: `audio/*` / `video/*` / `image/*`
  * Document: `text/html` / `application/pdf` / `text/markdown`
    (HTML / PDF / Markdown — for blog drafts, research notes,
    articles the user attached to feed `source=blog`)
Anything else returns `400 unsupported_asset_type`.

**Three request shapes**:
  * `multipart/form-data` with `file=@/path/to/asset` — the standard
    multipart form upload. Best for SDKs / curl / Postman / ChatGPT
    Custom GPT Action. Server cap 500 MB. Returns
    `AssetResponse { object:"asset", url, ... }` — bytes are already
    on S3 and the URL resolves immediately.
  * `application/json` with `{ mode: "presign", filename,
    content_type }` — **the path the MCP tool dispatches through**
    (the MCP transport can't carry binary). Server mints a
    1-hour-lived pre-signed S3 PUT URL; the caller then `PUT`s the
    bytes straight to S3. Returns
    `AssetPresignResponse { object:"asset_presign", put_url, get_url, ... }`.
    The `get_url` resolves for 24 hours after the PUT lands. The
    signature binds **only the host** — the caller does NOT need to
    echo back any Content-Type / metadata header. `headers_required`
    is empty by design so `curl -X PUT --upload-file <file>
    "<put_url>"` works as-is across HTTP clients.
  * `application/json` with `{ file_data: <base64>, filename,
    content_type }` — legacy / small-file convenience for callers
    that already have the bytes inline and don't want a second
    request. Server cap 500 MB decoded; in practice the MCP
    transport caps tool args to ~25 MB, so MCP agents use the
    `mode:"presign"` shape instead.

file.description: The audio / video / image / document (HTML / PDF / Markdown) file to upload.

200.description:
Upload succeeded (multipart / base64 → `AssetResponse`) OR
pre-signed URL minted (presign → `AssetPresignResponse`).

Synchronous, free. Self-notify only — the recipient (email address +
Telegram chat) is resolved server-side from the account that owns

**Multi-channel delivery**:

    has an email on file. `subject` becomes the email subject line.
  * **telegram** — an ADDITIONAL channel. When the user has also
    completed `Connect Telegram` at https://widecast.ai/#setup, the
    SAME notification is ALSO sent to their Telegram chat, with
    `subject` prepended in **bold** before the body.

The response carries `delivery: [...]` — the channels that were
delivered successfully (e.g. `["email","telegram"]` or `["email"]`)
— plus per-channel `email` / `telegram` objects with their own
status. `status` is `"sent"` when every attempted channel
succeeded, `"partial"` when at least one but not all succeeded.

Edge cases:
  * No email on file but Telegram connected → Telegram only; the
    response includes a `note` + `setup_url`.
  * Neither email nor Telegram → 400 `no_delivery_channel`.

Rate-limited to 60 notifications/hour/account.

Payload modes:
  * **text** — `subject` + `message`.
  * **photo** — `message` is the caption, `photo_url` a public
    http(s) URL (Telegram downloads it; email embeds it inline).
  * **video** — `message` is the caption, `video_url` a public
    http(s) URL (Telegram downloads it; email shows a link).

`photo_url` and `video_url` are mutually exclusive. `parse_mode` is
opt-in (`Markdown` / `MarkdownV2` / `HTML`) and formats the body;
omit for plain text. On Telegram, if the bold subject + body exceeds
Telegram's byte limit the Telegram channel is skipped (email is
still sent) — reported as `telegram.status: "skipped"`.

example.subject: Your video is ready
example.message: All 8 scenes finished rendering — open the editor to review.

200.description: Notification delivered on at least one channel.

400.description:
`missing_field` (subject/message), `subject_too_long`,
`invalid_parse_mode`, `conflicting_media`,
`invalid_photo_url`/`invalid_video_url`, `message_too_long`, or
`no_delivery_channel` (no email AND no Telegram on the account).

502.description: `notification_send_failed` — every attempted channel failed (`details` carries per-channel errors).

post.summary: Mint a no-login client link and optionally notify the client.
post.description:
Synchronous, free. Mint a no-login client link ("magic link") and
OPTIONALLY send it through the account's notification channels.
Built for autonomous AI agents operating an account: e.g. after
finishing a video, send the client a `record` link; after queueing
an idea, send a `content_plan` link so the client can review.

**Link types** (`link_type`):
  * **record** — opens one specific project's recording workspace
    (REQUIRES `topic_id`).
  * **content_plan** — the Saved Ideas / content-plan screen.
  * **setup** — the account Setup Center.
  * **social_dashboard** — the Social Dashboard (statistics).
  * **publish_schedule** — the Publish Schedule screen.

**Mint-only vs notify**: when `channels` is omitted, empty, or
all-false, NO notification is sent — the caller gets `magic_url`
back and decides later (mint-only). When at least one channel is
`true`, the link is delivered on those channels and the response
carries a per-channel `results` object.

Recipients are ALWAYS resolved server-side from the account's
Setup > Notification settings — the caller can NEVER supply a
phone number or email address (anti-spam-relay design).

Notification content is composed SERVER-SIDE per `link_type`
(`record` includes the video's title/hook; `content_plan` says
"Your content plan is ready for review"; etc.) across the Telegram
message, SMS (Twilio) and email with a CTA button.

record_with_channels.summary: Mint a record link for one project and notify via Telegram + email

content_plan_mint_only.summary: Mint a content-plan link only (no notification sent)

200.description: Link minted (and, when channels were requested, delivery attempted).

400.description:
`invalid_json`, `invalid_link_type` (param=link_type),
`missing_field` (param=topic_id, when `link_type=record`
without a `topic_id`), `invalid_topic_id` (param=topic_id), or
`invalid_channels` (param=channels).

409.description:
`script_not_saved` (param=topic_id) — `link_type=record` and the
video has no saved script on the server yet, so the link would open
on an empty waiting screen. Save the script first, then create the
client link.

500.description: `client_link_failed` — the API key has no account email.

post.summary: Report a WideCast problem to the WideCast team.
post.description:
Synchronous, free. Report a problem with WideCast itself — a failing
upload, a broken export, an overlay that will not build, an endpoint
returning a 5xx you cannot work around. The report is emailed
straight to the WideCast team.

The account (company + email) is resolved server-side from the API
key and is **never** accepted in the request body.

**This is not a user-notification channel.** To tell the *user*
something, use [`POST /v1/notification/send`](#operation/sendNotification).
And do not use it for content problems you can fix yourself (a weak
hook, a wrong background, a typo) — only for WideCast malfunctioning.

Whenever the failing call returned a `request_id`, put it in
`context` — it is the single most useful field for tracing a report
back to the server-side log.

Shares its core (`_wc_normalize_error_report` + `_report_error_core`)
with the dashboard's `/report_error` route, so a report renders
identically whichever surface submitted it.

Each report also opens an `auto` ticket (or counts a repeat on the open
one) that the account can follow with [`listTickets`](#operation/listTickets).

context.attempted: second export retry after scene 4 edit

200.description: Report delivered to the WideCast team.

400.description:
`missing_field` (`error_message` empty), `error_message_too_long`,
`module_too_long`, `invalid_module` (not a string), or
`invalid_context` (not an object).

502.description: `error_report_failed` — the report could not be delivered.

post.summary: File a problem ticket for the WideCast team.
post.description:
Free. For a WideCast problem the owner hit while working with you: an error, a page
that does not work, a setup step that fails. The guide for agents is
https://widecast.ai/agent/tickets.md: gather the fields, show the owner the whole
ticket in one block, and send it only when they say yes.

The account comes from the API key, never from the body. Text that looks like a key,
token, password or cookie is refused with `secret_in_ticket`; the value is never
echoed. The same problem filed again while its ticket is open is counted on that
ticket (`duplicate: true`) instead of opening a new one. At most 10 tickets an hour
and 30 a day per account, repeats included.

The WideCast team answers inside the ticket; the account hears of every reply or
status change through its usual WideCast notifications. Follow it with
[`getTicket`](#operation/getTicket).

example.title: Approvals page shows an empty card after Pick
example.expected: The idea brief opens so I can choose Video script
example.actual: The card turns blank and its buttons disappear
example.boss_words: I clicked pick and the card went white
example.error: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'brief')

200.description: Filed, or counted on the open ticket of the same problem.

400.description:
`secret_in_ticket` (`error.param` names the field, `error.details.kind` what it
looked like: remove it and send again), `missing_field` (`title`, or both `actual`
and `error` empty), `unknown_field`, `invalid_field`, `field_too_long`
(`error.details.max_chars`) or `invalid_request` (not a JSON object).

503.description: `tickets_unavailable`: try again shortly.

get.summary: List this account's tickets, most recently changed first.
get.description:
Free. The account's own tickets, including the `auto` tickets opened by
[`reportError`](#operation/reportError). Use it when the owner asks about a problem
they reported or forwards a WideCast notice about a ticket.

400.description: `invalid_status` or `invalid_limit`.

get.summary: Read one ticket with the WideCast team's replies and the next step.
get.description:
Free. `next_step` says in one sentence what to do now: answer a question
([`commentTicket`](#operation/commentTicket)), or update WideCast to `fixed_in` and
confirm the fix ([`verifyTicket`](#operation/verifyTicket)). Another account's
ticket answers 404.

404.description: `ticket_not_found`.

post.summary: Answer the WideCast team inside a ticket.
post.description:
Free. Add what the team asked for, or something new about the problem. Show the
owner anything that speaks for them before you send it. At most 30 comments an hour
per account; a `verified` or `closed` ticket takes no more comments.

example.text: It happens on every idea card, in Chrome and Safari, since this morning.

200.description: The ticket with the new comment.

400.description: `missing_field`, `field_too_long`, `unknown_field` or `secret_in_ticket`.

404.description: `ticket_not_found`.

409.description: `ticket_closed` (file a new ticket) or `ticket_full`.

post.summary: Tell the WideCast team whether the fix works.
post.description:
Free. Only for a `fixed` ticket: update WideCast to `fixed_in` or later, try the
same thing again with the owner, then send the result with the release you now run.
`works` marks the ticket `verified`; `still_broken` reopens it.

example.note: The brief opens after Pick again.

400.description: `missing_field`, `invalid_field` (`result`), `field_too_long` or `secret_in_ticket`.

404.description: `ticket_not_found`.

409.description:
`not_fixed` (the ticket is not `fixed` yet) or `update_first` (`release_id` is
older than `error.details.fixed_in`: update WideCast, then try again).

post.summary: Publish a video / blog / text to connected social platforms.
post.description:
Distribute content to the social platforms connected to your account
(via Upload-Post). Provide **exactly one** content mode:

- `topic_id` — publish a WideCast video OR blog/social post you already
  created (`/v1/create_video` or `/v1/create_content`). Auto-detects
  article vs video. A video must be finished (export the final MP4 with
  `/v1/export_video` first) else `publish_not_ready` (409).
- `text` — post arbitrary text (optionally with `photo_urls`).
- `video_url` — a **direct video file URL** (mp4/mov/…) to post; requires
  `title`. WideCast downloads it, then publishes.

`platforms` defaults to **all connected** platforms of the chosen
channel group. Charges 1 credit.

`channel_group` (integer, default 0 = primary) selects which CHANNEL
GROUP — a separate set of connected accounts, e.g. "Vietnamese
channels" vs "English channels" — the post goes through. One call
publishes through ONE group; list groups with `GET /v1/channel_groups`.

Publishing is asynchronous on the platform side: this returns the
upstream `request_ids` immediately (HTTP 202). Poll
`GET /v1/status/{request_id}` for per-platform post URLs. An article
spanning text + photo platforms may return up to two `request_ids`.

topic.summary: Publish an existing WideCast video to two platforms

text.summary: Post arbitrary text to all connected platforms

value.text: We just shipped v2 — try it free today!

external_video.summary: Post an external video file URL

channel_group.summary: Publish through the second channel group (e.g. English channels)

202.description: Publish accepted — poll the returned request_id(s).

get.summary: List the account's recent videos.
get.description: Synchronous, read-only, free. Returns recent videos/scripts (20 per page).

post.summary: Read structured scene data (data-first audit/edit entry point).
post.description:
Synchronous, free. **First step for data-first scene audit/edit** —
call this before `/v1/modify_scene` or `/v1/scene_inspector`.

**URL-RESPONSE CONTRACT** (default `delivery_mode="download_url"`):
the HTTP response is a small JSON envelope; the full video_data tree
(annotated `segments[]`, `scene_identity`, `global_settings`,
Remotion spec metadata) is published to a temporary public JSON file
on `origin.widecast.ai` and the envelope carries `data.url` +
`data.bytes` + `data.expires_at` + `data.ttl_seconds=900` (15-min
TTL) plus a 3-step `instructions` block. The agent must
`mkdir -p ./.widecast-video-data && cd ./.widecast-video-data` +
`curl -fsSL '<data.url>' -o video_data.json` + Read locally — the
full tree is NOT inlined in the HTTP response. This bypasses MCP
per-tool-call output caps that previously truncated 50–300 KB
payloads mid-JSON. Every call publishes a NEW unique file (token =
16 hex chars), so URLs are never reused — matches the realtime
semantics of video data. Host is `origin.widecast.ai` (CF-bypassed)
+ `?v=<mtime>` cache-bust. Server only responds AFTER the JSON is
fsynced + atomically renamed to its final path, so the URL is
guaranteed readable when the agent fetches it (no race). Operators
can flip to legacy inline mode via env flag
`WIDECAST_VIDEO_DATA_DELIVERY_MODE=inline_content` — in that mode
the HTTP response carries the full tree inline as before.

The published JSON file shape is the same as the legacy inline
response. To keep MCP payloads usable the API trims per-segment
`words` timing arrays, top-level `captions`, and internal
preview-cache fields (`savedVideos`, `savedImages`,
`_previewInstanceId`, `_remotionSpecFetching`,
`_forceNarratorRefit`). UI routes still get full data; this is the
agent-safe slim view.

**Scene identity rule** (also returned as `scene_identity` in the
response): use `voice_file` as the stable per-scene UID.
`segment.id` is only display/order metadata and may change after
reorder/add/delete. The Remotion spec for a scene is
`{voice_file}_spec.json`.

**Per-segment fields agents care about**:
  * `voice_file` (stable scene UID; use for modify/inspect).
  * `id` / `order_id` / `scene_index` (current order; UNSTABLE).
  * `type` (`A-roll` | `B-roll` | `thumbnail`).
  * `text` (narration), `talking_point`, `visual`, `quote`,
    `keyword`.
  * `mediaUrl`, `mediaType`, `thumbnailUrl`, `videoTrim`.
  * `overlay.caption`, `overlay.narrator` — legacy 280×498 editor
    preview coordinates.
  * `remotion_spec` — `"none"` means the user intentionally
    disabled the overlay on that scene; agents must NOT auto-edit
    or re-enable unless the user asks.
  * `remotion_spec_file` — `{voice_file}_spec.json`.
  * `remotion_spec_url` — cache-busted
    `https://widecast.ai/downloads/{company_id}/{topic_id}/{voice_file}_spec.json?v={mtime}`;
    present only when `remotion_spec_state="ready"`.
  * `remotion_spec_version`, `remotion_spec_exists`,
    `remotion_spec_state` (`ready` | `missing` | `disabled`).
  * `agent_meta` — same metadata bundled for quick consumption
    (`stable_scene_id`, `coordinate_spaces`, `scene_index`, etc.).

**Coordinate warning**: Remotion spec objects use **720×1280
canvas** coordinates; legacy `overlay.caption` and
`overlay.narrator` use **280×498 editor preview** coordinates. Pass
`coordinate_space` to `/v1/modify_scene`'s `remotion.group.rect`
accordingly.

**Remotion spec is NOT inlined** — it can carry large base64
images. Fetch `remotion_spec_url` only when
`remotion_spec_state="ready"` and you actually need object-level
overlay boxes; otherwise use the metadata only.

**Internal poster diagnostics are stripped by default.** Per-segment
`remotion_poster_file`, `remotion_poster_url`,
`remotion_poster_version`, `remotion_poster_state`,
`remotion_poster_exists`, and `remotion_poster_warnings` (and
their copies inside `agent_meta.remotion_spec`) describe the
server-side `{voice_file}_overlay_poster.png` used by
`/v1/scene_inspector` fallback. Pass
`include_diagnostics: true` to surface them for server/debug
audits.

Mirrors the same engine the dashboard's scene editor uses on open
(rebalance A/B rolls + ensure background music + persist if
changed), so the data here matches what the user sees in
`#scene_editor?topic_id=…` exactly.

video_id.description:
Topic id from `/v1/create_video` / scene_editor. Accepts
`widecast...`, `gubo...`, or current topic ids. Same id
used by `/v1/status`, `/v1/export_video`,
`/v1/modify_scene`, `/v1/scene_inspector`.

include_diagnostics.description:
Optional debug flag. When `true`, per-segment
`remotion_poster_*` diagnostic keys (and their
copies inside `agent_meta.remotion_spec`) are
returned. Default is `false` because those keys
describe the server-side poster used by scene
inspector fallback — agents don't act on them.

404.description:
`video_not_found` — no video with this id on the account. Check
the id is the topic_id returned by `/v1/create_video` and that
it belongs to the API key's account.

409.description:
`script_not_ready` — video is still processing or never had a
script generated. Poll `/v1/status` until
`status=="completed"`, then retry.

500.description:
`video_data_publish_failed` — the response tree was assembled
but could not be persisted to disk (no readable URL to return).

502.description:
`script_parse_failed` — stored video_script is malformed.
Contact support with the request_id.

post.summary: Live browser inspector — expensive last-resort, use AFTER scene_geometry.
post.description:
Synchronous live browser inspector. **More expensive than
`/v1/scene_geometry`** — use only when data + geometry are not
enough: typically when the agent needs browser truth (mounted DOM,
computed boxes, current preview play state) or a small 280×498
visual screenshot for aesthetic judgment. Do NOT use as the first
step if `/v1/scene_geometry` already gives the boxes you need.

**How it works**: server broadcasts a tiny MQTT probe to every
open editor tab for this video, elects ONE healthy foreground /
active browser within ~800ms, then sends the real inspector
command only to that tab. `/v1/modify_scene` realtime broadcasts
to all editors separately — this tool's election only affects
which tab returns the live inspection. Presence alone is not
usability: tabs on the workflow page, on a different video, or
any page without a mounted scene preview are ignored for scene-
bound commands.

**`screenshot_scene_280x498` response shape — temporary public
URL.** On success (live editor capture OR server-fallback
composite from thumbnails + `{voice_file}_overlay_poster.png`),
the HTTP response is a regular JSON `SceneInspectorResponse`
whose `result.screenshot` carries a *temporary public URL* —
NOT bytes, NOT base64:

  * `url` — `https://origin.widecast.ai/downloads/<co>/<topic>/inspector/<voice>_<token>.jpg?v=<mtime>`.
    Fetch the JPEG bytes with `curl <url>`. No
    `Authorization` header required — the path is served
    publicly by nginx. The host is ``origin.widecast.ai`` (not
    ``widecast.ai``) — bypasses Cloudflare so 15-min ephemeral
    URLs never get pinned in CF edge cache. The cache-bust
    ``?v=<mtime>`` is belt-and-suspenders.
  * `mime_type` — `image/jpeg`.
  * `width` / `height` — pixel dimensions (typically 280 / 498).
  * `bytes` — JPEG byte length on disk.
  * `expires_at` — ISO 8601 UTC; the URL is guaranteed
    readable until this moment.
  * `ttl_seconds` — `900` (15 minutes).

Every call publishes a fresh unique file (16-hex token), so
the URL is never reused across calls — matches the realtime
semantics of inspector data. The server only responds after
the JPEG is `fsync`-ed and atomically renamed to its final
path, so the URL is guaranteed readable when the agent reads
the response (no race).

**All other actions still return JSON
`SceneInspectorResponse`** as before.

**No live editor → graceful behaviour**:
  - For non-screenshot actions, the response is HTTP 200 with
    `status: "unavailable"` and `code: "no_live_editor"` (no
    presence) or `"no_active_editor"` (presence but unresponsive).
    Fall back to `/v1/video_data` + `/v1/scene_geometry` +
    fetching `remotion_spec_url`.
  - `screenshot_scene_280x498` and `overlay_poster` are always
    served via the same 15-minute URL contract whether or not a
    live editor was elected — both are pure server-side
    compositors.

**`overlay_poster` — audit the overlay in isolation.** Companion
action to `screenshot_scene_280x498`. The server composites ONLY
the Remotion overlay poster on a solid black 280×498 canvas (no
background image, no narrator, no caption). Purpose: catch
text-quality issues the composite screenshot hides —
readability, typos, grammar, semantic drift, missing Vietnamese
diacritics, glyph rendering (□ tofu, cut characters),
punctuation. Response shape mirrors screenshot but uses
`result.overlay_poster.{url, mime_type, width, height, bytes,
expires_at, ttl_seconds}` and adds `result.review_checklist` —
a English reminder that walks the agent through 8 audit
dimensions. Filename is STABLE (`<voice>_poster.jpg`,
overwritten each call); the `?v=<mtime>` cache-bust bumps every
write so the URL string is fresh in every response. Server
still fsync+atomic-renames BEFORE responding so the file is
guaranteed readable. Errors specific to overlay_poster: 409
`overlay_not_available` (scene has no poster —
`remotion_spec="none"` or spec not yet built), 500
`overlay_publish_failed` (disk write / rename failed).

**Actions** (`action`):
  * `list_live_editors` — presence list of open editor tabs
    (browser / OS / last_seen) — debug/discovery only.
  * `list_instances` — preview instance ids mounted in the elected
    tab.
  * `get_preview_state` — current playing/paused/scene/time in the
    preview player.
  * `get_scene_dom_snapshot` — DOM subtree for a scene (scoped via
    optional `selector` — keep narrow).
  * `get_computed_boxes` — `getBoundingClientRect` for scene
    elements. **Prefer `/v1/scene_geometry` for structural
    audits** — it is cheaper, always-available (no browser
    needed), and returns the same boxes plus collision violations
    and safe zones in pure JSON.
  * `screenshot_scene_280x498` — small JPEG (~280×498) showing
    the FULL composite: background + Remotion overlay poster +
    narrator + caption. **Response is JSON with a 15-minute
    public URL** (see above). Fetch the bytes with
    `curl <result.screenshot.url>`.
  * `overlay_poster` — small JPEG (~280×498) showing ONLY the
    overlay poster on solid black. **Response is JSON with a
    URL + a `review_checklist` reminder** — use to catch
    typos / diacritic loss / glyph tofu / grammar / semantic
    drift the background image would otherwise mask.
  * `activate_scene` — bring the elected tab to scene N (may
    visibly switch the editor for that user).
  * `reload_preview` / `pause_preview` / `play_preview` /
    `seek_preview` — preview transport controls.

**No arbitrary JavaScript eval is exposed.** Use `voice_file` as
the scene selector wherever possible.

presence.summary: Check who has the editor open

boxes.summary: Computed bounding boxes for one scene

screenshot.summary: Small 280×498 capture — JSON response with 15-minute public URL
screenshot.description:
Response is a regular `SceneInspectorResponse` whose
`result.screenshot.url` is a public path the agent
fetches with `curl` (no auth header). The URL is
unique per call and valid for 15 minutes.

overlay_poster.summary: Overlay only on solid black — audit typos / diacritics / glyph rendering
overlay_poster.description:
Response carries `result.overlay_poster.url` (public,
valid 15 min) + `result.review_checklist` — a
English reminder for the agent to walk 8 audit
dimensions (readability / typos / grammar /
semantic / diacritic / glyph / numbers / punctuation).
Filename is stable (`<voice>_poster.jpg`) but
`?v=<mtime>` freshens the URL every call.

200.description:
Inspector outcome. Always JSON `SceneInspectorResponse`:
  * **`screenshot_scene_280x498`** → JSON carrying
    `result.screenshot.{url, mime_type, width, height,
    bytes, expires_at, ttl_seconds}`. The agent fetches
    the JPEG by `curl <result.screenshot.url>` — the URL
    is public, fresh per call, and valid 15 minutes.
  * **`overlay_poster`** → JSON carrying
    `result.overlay_poster.{url, mime_type, width,
    height, bytes, expires_at, ttl_seconds}` plus
    `result.review_checklist` — a English reminder
    covering readability / typos / grammar / semantic /
    diacritic / glyph / numbers / punctuation. Filename
    is stable (`<voice>_poster.jpg`); `?v=<mtime>` bumps
    every call. Fetch bytes with
    `curl <result.overlay_poster.url>`.
  * **All other actions** → JSON `SceneInspectorResponse`
    with `status` discriminating:
      * `"completed"` — elected tab returned a `result`.
      * `"unavailable"` — no editor available; `code` is
        `no_live_editor` (no presence) or `no_active_editor`
        (presence but unresponsive).
      * `"error"` — browser-side failure; `code` carries the
        provider error.

400.description:
`unsupported_action` (not in the action enum) or
`publisher_missing` (server MQTT publisher unavailable).

404.description: `video_not_found` — no video with this id on the account.

409.description:
* `script_not_ready` — video still processing or never had
  a script generated (compositor needs the video_script).
* `overlay_not_available` — `overlay_poster` action only.
  The scene has no Remotion overlay poster to render —
  either the overlay was disabled
  (`segment.remotion_spec="none"`) or the spec has not been
  built yet. Upload an overlay first (see
  `/v1/modify_scene` Upload Overlay branch), then retry.

500.description:
* `screenshot_publish_failed` — screenshot was composed but
  could not be persisted to disk (no readable URL to
  return).
* `overlay_publish_failed` — `overlay_poster` JPEG was
  composed but could not be persisted (no readable URL to
  return).

get.summary: Account profile + remaining credits.
get.description: Synchronous, read-only, free.

avatar_video.description:
`true` when the plan allows AI-presenter ("avatar") videos
(`POST /v1/create_video` with `presenter: true`); `false` on Free / Trial
(and expired) accounts, which can make faceless videos only.

avatar_ready.description:
`true` when at least one usable photo set (camera set) exists. Independent of the
plan. Create it in WideCast Setup (https://widecast.ai/#setup).

voice_clone_ready.description:
`true` when a cloned voice exists. Independent of the plan. Create it in
WideCast Setup (https://widecast.ai/#setup).

connected_platforms.description: Platforms connected in ANY channel group (de-duplicated, primary first). Per-group lists live in `channel_groups`; with a single group this is exactly that group's list.

channel_groups.description: Every channel group (primary first) with its connected platforms.

get.summary: Solo Agency tier for this key (Ed25519-signed JWS, 24h).
get.description:
Synchronous, read-only, free. Used by the Solo Agency bridge (and its
Chrome extension) to enforce plan limits offline: the bridge caches the
raw `token` and re-verifies its EdDSA signature against the public key
from `/v1/solo/pubkey`. `tier` follows the account's WideCast plan —
Free · Starter · Pro · Business · Enterprise (each tier's price and limits ride in the token's `ladder` claim, from the server's plans.json) — unless
an operator grant overrides it; an expired WideCast plan yields `free`.
`limits` (0 = unlimited; max_groups / max_campaigns are per client) and
`features` (enrich, write_actions, harvest, zillow, …) are what the

## ⚠ Download-zip delivery mode (experiment, 2026-06-30)

The endpoint does **not** return skill content inline. Instead
the response is a 4-step download instruction (per format):

1. `mkdir -p ./.widecast-skill-<format-folder> && cd ./.widecast-skill-<format-folder>`
   (folder name follows `result.download.work_dir`)
2. `curl -fsSL <result.download.zip_url> -o <filename>.zip`
3. (optional) `shasum -a 256 <filename>.zip` matches
   `result.download.sha256`
4. `unzip -o <filename>.zip`

Then `Read('<work_dir>/<format-folder>/SKILL.md')` and follow
its LOAD MAP. For `format='video'`, sub-modules are `method` /
`formats` / `hooks` / `ctas` / `research_visuals` / `handoff`.
For `format='blog'` and `format='social'`, the skill is a single
SKILL.md today.

Per-format zips (hosted at `origin.widecast.ai`, CF-bypassed):
* `video-script-writing.zip` (~30 KB)
* `blog-writing.zip` (~5 KB)
* `social-post-writing.zip` (~3 KB)

**Why this mode**: agent step-adherence (research-first,
fictional-frame factual-core, image vetting, hand-off order) is
measurably better when content is read from a local file than
from a tool result. The skill content on disk is identical to
previous inline-content mode — only the delivery mechanism
changed.

## Always-returned `contract` field

Every response carries a short (~1.4 KB) `contract` field with
the cross-cutting rules. Read it FIRST as the safety net for
cross-cutting rules.

## Host requirements

Local shell + `curl` + `unzip` + a file-reading tool. On hosts
where bash sandbox FS is separate from the file-tool FS, use
`cat` via bash.

## Maintainer workflow

Drop `.md` under `widecast/skills/<format>-writing/` (or in the
format root for blog/social), then `bash deploy_widecast.sh`.
No Flask restart needed for content-only changes; server mtime-
caches the zip.

## Reverting to inline-content mode

Set env `WIDECAST_WRITING_DELIVERY_MODE=inline_content` +
restart Flask. Inline path with `available_modules[]` +
per-module `?module=<id>` lazy-load is retained as fallback.

* `social` — platform caption (X / LinkedIn / IG / TikTok / FB /

## ⚠ Download-zip delivery mode (experiment, 2026-06-30)

The endpoint does **not** return skill content inline. Instead
the response carries (a) a `preload_tools` hint block and (b) a
4-step download instruction.

### Step 0 — preload the WideCast toolkit (skip → edit will fail mid-run)

Some MCP hosts (Codex, Claude Code) lazy-load tool schemas via
their `ToolSearch` mechanism and default to **narrow keyword
queries**. If the agent's initial search misses a tool it later
needs (e.g. `widecast_modify_scene`), the edit run either fails
mid-flow or silently skips the edit. To prevent this, every
response carries a `preload_tools` block:

- `preload_tools.one_shot_query` — a literal
  `select:widecast_video_data,widecast_scene_geometry,...`
  string. Copy verbatim into your `ToolSearch` call's `query`
  param; one round-trip loads every edit-flow tool at once.
- `preload_tools.broad_query` — fallback keyword query
  (`widecast`) for hosts that don't support `select:` syntax.
- `preload_tools.broad_max_results` — max_results to pass with
  `broad_query`; auto-scales with the tool count.
- `preload_tools.tools[]` — every tool with a 1-line reason,
  first sentence of the tool's own MCP description.

The list is **auto-derived from the live MCP registry at
request time**, so adding a new WideCast tool later is
zero-config — the field auto-includes it.

The `preload_tools` block ships in BOTH delivery modes
(download_zip and inline_content).

### Then — download the zip

1. `mkdir -p ./.widecast-skill-video-editing && cd ./.widecast-skill-video-editing`
2. `curl -fsSL <result.download.zip_url> -o video-editing.zip`
3. (optional) `shasum -a 256 video-editing.zip` matches
   `result.download.sha256`
4. `unzip -o video-editing.zip`

Then `Read('./.widecast-skill-video-editing/video-editing/SKILL.md')`
and follow its LOAD MAP. The skill content on disk is
identical to the previous inline-content mode (master
`SKILL.md` ~14 KB INDEX + 5 core modules
`01_critical_rules` / `02_jump_prevention` / `03_dod_gates` /
`04_principles_workflow` / `05_quality_qa_priority` +
per-scene modules + style libs).

**Why this mode**: agent step-adherence (background audit,
screenshot show-local, gate verdicts, module reload) is
measurably better when the playbook is read from a local file
than from a tool result. Local-file path forces full reading
+ re-reading at each step; tool-result path tends to be
skimmed once.

## Always-returned `contract` field

Every response carries a short (~1.5 KB) `contract` field with
the cross-cutting rules — selector = `voice_file`, autonomous
end-to-end run, screenshot evidence, SVG overlay rules, 9-gate
DoD, lazy-load contract. **Read `contract` first as the safety
net**, then run the download + read SKILL.md from disk.

## Host requirements

Your runtime MUST have a local shell + `curl` + `unzip` + a
file-reading tool (`Read('<path>')` if your host reads
arbitrary files; `cat <path>` via bash if `Read` is restricted
to project files). On hosts where the bash sandbox FS is
separate from the file-tool FS, use `cat` via bash — content
identical, only the access tool differs.

## Maintainer workflow

- Drop a new `.md` file under `widecast/skills/video-editing/`
  (root or `ai_video_editor/` or `ai_video_editor/styles/`).
- Run `bash deploy_widecast.sh` — the build script
  auto-rebuilds `video-editing.zip` via `_zip_skills()`.
- **No Flask restart needed for content-only updates** — the
  server's `_wc_editing_zip_meta()` mtime-caches the zip; new
  mtime → new sha256 → new `?v=<mtime>` URL. Agent's next call
  downloads the fresh zip automatically.
- Restart Flask only when `dashboard2.py` itself changes (env
  var, route logic, helper rename) or when the delivery-mode
  env flag flips.

## Reverting to inline-content mode

Set env `WIDECAST_EDITING_DELIVERY_MODE=inline_content` +
restart Flask. The previous multi-module inline-content code
path (with `available_modules[]` + per-module `?module=<id>`
lazy-load) is retained as fallback.

## Module IDs (inline-content mode only)

Hierarchical filesystem path WITHOUT the `.md` extension. Each
path segment must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$`. Examples:
`ai_video_editor/10_mechanics`,
`ai_video_editor/styles/text_axes`. `../` and hidden segments
are rejected with 400 `invalid_module_id`. **In download_zip
mode (the default), the `module` query param is parsed but
ignored** — every call returns the same download instruction.

## Freshness

- Download URL is cache-busted with `?v=<mtime>` per request;
  new deploy → new mtime → new URL → fresh content.
- Response carries `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- Zip hosted at `origin.widecast.ai` (Cloudflare-bypassed),
  so there is no CDN layer to worry about.

post.summary: Count the drafts that wait for the owner.
post.description: Returns how many community drafts wait for the owner's decision, in total and per client. Read-only. Matches the Communities line on the Approvals page.

- `solo_community_unavailable` - Communities is not installed on the server.
- `storage_error` - The store could not be reached. Try again shortly.

post.summary: Decide a community draft: save, approve, schedule, move, now, skip, make a new picture or cancel.
post.description: Acts on one draft of a community post. `save` keeps an edited `text`. `approve` (with the text as shown) puts the post in the destination's next free slot inside the community's own hours; the draft's picture must be ready. `schedule` approves it for the time in `send_at`, which must be inside the account's posting hours (the community's own window does not apply), 60 seconds to 180 days ahead. `move` gives an approved post that has not gone out a new `send_at` (same checks). `now` puts an approved post that has not gone out at the server's own now plus 60 seconds (`send_at` is not needed), through the same posting-hours check: outside the hours it answers `outside_posting_hours` with `opens_at`. `skip` drops a draft that waits. `image` makes a new picture (one credit; an optional `image_prompt` replaces the prompt) for a draft that waits. `cancel` takes an approved post that has not gone out out of the schedule. The answer is the draft. Matches the draft buttons on the Communities page (the page route is `/solo/communities/draft`).

client.description: The client slug the item belongs to, for example `acme-dental`. The slugs of the account are listed in the `clients` field of the feature's `state` operation.

id.description: The draft id (`cd_` followed by 26 characters), from `drafts` of `communities_get`.

action.description: What to do with the draft.

text.description: The post's text as it should go out (at most 5,000 characters). With `save` or `approve` it replaces the draft's text; only a draft that waits can change text.

image_prompt.description: `image` only: a new picture prompt, at most 1,000 characters.

send_at.description: When to send, in one of three forms: an ISO 8601 string with a UTC offset or `Z` (`2026-11-20T09:00:00+07:00`), an ISO 8601 string without an offset (`2026-11-20T09:00`, read as wall-clock time in `tz`, which is then required), or whole epoch seconds. The time must be at least 60 seconds from now and at most 180 days ahead.

tz.description: An IANA time zone name such as `America/Los_Angeles`. Required when `send_at` has no UTC offset; otherwise it only sets the zone the time is shown in. When left out, the account owner's zone is shown.

example.text: Three habits that help kids brush longer.

400.description:
- `invalid_client` - `client` is missing or is not a valid client slug (`param: client`).
- `invalid_request` - `action` is not one of the eight values (`param: action`), or `text` is empty or too long.
- `send_at_invalid` - `send_at` is not an ISO 8601 date and time or epoch seconds (`param: send_at`).
- `tz_unknown` - `send_at` has no UTC offset and `tz` is missing or is not a time zone name this server knows (`param: tz`).
- `send_at_past` - `send_at` is less than 60 seconds from now (`param: send_at`).
- `send_at_too_far` - `send_at` is more than 180 days from now (`param: send_at`).
- `outside_posting_hours` - The chosen instant is outside the account's posting hours. The error object also carries `opens_at` (epoch seconds of the next opening after that instant) and `posting_hours` (`start`, `end`, `tz`).

404.description: - `draft_not_found` - No draft with that `id` for this client (`param: id`).

409.description:
- `not_waiting` - The draft does not wait for a decision any more (`save` with text, `approve`, `schedule`, `skip` and `image` need a waiting draft).
- `image_not_ready` - `approve` or `schedule`: the picture is not ready; make a new picture first.
- `not_scheduled` - `move`, `now` or `cancel`: the post is not approved and waiting to go out.
- `no_slot` - `approve`: no posting time is free in the next year.
- `busy` - The draft changed a moment ago. Open it again.

500.description: - `solo_internal_error` - An unexpected failure on the server. The request id in the answer identifies it.

503.description:
- `posting_hours_unavailable` - The posting hours could not be read right now. Try again shortly.
- `solo_community_unavailable` - Communities is not installed on the server.
- `storage_error` - The store could not be reached. Try again shortly.

post.summary: Read the owner's time zone, the posting hours and the schedule limits.
post.description: Returns what a schedule picker needs: the account owner's time zone `tz` (and where it came from), the current local time, the posting hours Facebook posts may go out in (`start`, `end`, `always`, whether they are `open` now, and the epoch times of the next opening and closing) and the limits of `send_at`: at least `min_ahead_s` (60) seconds and at most `max_ahead_days` (180) days from now. Email can be scheduled at any hour; Facebook posts (Post broadcast and Communities) only inside the posting hours. When `tz` (the caller's own zone) is a valid zone name it is recorded first as the owner's zone hint. Never fails because the hours cannot be read: the zone is then `UTC` and `open` is null. Matches the schedule picker of the three pages.

client.description: The client slug whose posting hours to read. Optional; the account's hours are used when left out.

tz.description: The caller's own IANA time zone, for example `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh`; recorded as the zone hint when valid.

503.description:

post.summary: List what is scheduled and what went out, across email, posts and communities.
post.description: Returns one list of sends of the three features: `when: upcoming` lists what is scheduled, soonest first; `when: past` lists what went out or ended, newest first. Each row says the kind, client, title, who it goes to, the time, the state, whether the page or an agent started it (`by`), the progress, what can still be done with it (`actions`: `move`, `now` and `cancel` as the actions of the matching `broadcast_schedule`, `groupposts_schedule` or `communities_decide`; all three accept the same three words) and the page link. A post send row has its copies in `children`. `kind` and `client` narrow the list. Paging: pass `next_cursor` of an answer as `cursor` to get the next page. When one feature cannot be read, its rows are left out and its kind is named in `partial`. Read-only. Matches the History page.

client.description: Only this client's sends.

next_cursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` for the next page; null when there is none.

partial.description: Kinds that could not be read; their rows are missing.

XRequestId.description: Unique ID for this request — include in any support ticket.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
Client-generated UUID. Two requests with the same key within 24h return
the SAME video and do NOT create a new one. **Read but not enforced
in pilot.**

CreateVideoRequest.description:
Conditional shape based on `source`:
  * source="text" (default) → `script_text` required.
  * source="idea" → `idea_text` required; `language`, `video_length`,
    `research_enabled` optional with defaults.
The other text field is ignored when not matching `source`.

script_approved.description:
Confirmation flag for AI agents calling via MCP or ChatGPT Action.
**MCP callers**: REQUIRED (the MCP wrapper rejects calls where this
is missing or false). **ChatGPT Action callers**: should set true
after showing the user the full hand-off and getting explicit
approval. **SDK / curl / Postman callers**: this field is ignored
by the REST endpoint; SDK consumers are trusted to handle their
own UX. The point of the flag is to enforce that the dialog flow
with the end user actually happened — a bare "make a video about X"
from the user is the REQUEST, not the approval.

production_mode.description:
User's explicit answer to the three-way production question.
Applies to source=text/idea/blog AND source=audio_url
(ignored for video sources — the footage IS the visuals — and
for `output_type="text"`, which makes no scenes).
Three valid values, each with a different downstream UX:
  * `faceless` — B-roll only, no narrator on screen. The video
    is fully automated; user just reviews and renders.
  * `face_clone` — the user's pre-trained Face clone + Voice
    clone speaks the script. The user **must have set both up
    at https://widecast.ai/#setup** before the render runs —
    if they haven't, the AI agent should point them there
    during the dialog.
  * `teleprompter` — the user records themselves reading the
    script via WideCast's built-in teleprompter (after the
    scenes prepare). No clone needed; user physically records.
