`faceless` maps to `faceless=true`. Both `face_clone` and
`teleprompter` produce a "normal" video (narrator on screen)
and map to `faceless=false` — the distinction is purely so the
AI agent tells the user the right next step.
**Audio-source nuance** (source=audio_url): the user's original
voice in the recording IS the narration in every mode — it is
never re-synthesized via TTS. `face_clone` here means the clone's
face is on screen lip-synced to the user's original audio (not
to a clone-voice resynthesis); the clone contributes only the
visual face, the voice stays the user's.
**Every caller** (MCP, ChatGPT Action, SDK, curl) may pass the
user's answer here: the REST endpoint performs the same mapping
as the MCP wrapper, so this field and `faceless` are two ways to
say the same thing. Sending both is fine only when they agree; a
contradiction (e.g. `production_mode: "face_clone"` with
`faceless: true`) or a value outside the enum → HTTP 400
`invalid_production_mode`. The effective value comes back in
the create response as `meta.faceless`.

source.description:
Discriminates the input flow:
  * `text` (default — backward-compat): provide `script_text`
    used VERBATIM by the narrator.
  * `idea`: provide `idea_text`; server writes a narration from
    the idea (AI) then continues into the same scene-sourcing
    pipeline as `text`.
  * `blog`: provide `blog_text` (an article to repurpose);
    identical pipeline to `idea`, just a longer input.
  * `video_url` / `audio_url`: provide `video_url` / `audio_url`
    — **any public http(s) URL**. Direct file links (S3, R2,
    transfer.sh, file.io, your own CDN — anywhere an AI agent or
    user can drop the file and copy back a URL) AND platform pages
    (YouTube / TikTok / Facebook) both work. Loopback / private /
    link-local hosts are rejected (`unsupported_media_url`).
    Media-ingest (A49) — the script already lives in the media.
    The footage becomes the B-roll (video) / the audio becomes
    the narration (audio).
  * `video_file` / `audio_file`: upload the media file. Send the
    request as **multipart/form-data** with the file in the
    `video_file` / `audio_file` part (mirrors the UI upload).
**AI agent path for "user attached a file in chat":** call
`POST /v1/upload_asset` first (or the MCP `widecast_upload_asset`
tool), get back a public S3 URL with a 24-hour TTL, then pass
that URL here as `audio_url` / `video_url`. Do NOT inline-base64.
`idea` and `blog` are generative sources — they support
`output_type: "text"` (stop at the editable script). Media sources
support `output_type: "text"` too = Remake (A50): extract the
transcript only, no footage/scene build.

script_text.description:
**Required when `source="text"`.** Plain text script — pasted
narration. Used VERBATIM by the narrator (no AI rewriting).
Bounds are LOCKED:
  * minimum 80 words (~20s of narration)
  * maximum 500 words (~120s / 2 min of narration)

Word count = whitespace split (`len(text.split())`) — works for
English + Vietnamese. Outside the bounds → HTTP 400 with
`error.code` = `script_too_short` / `script_too_long`.

**Inline media (use your own images/videos).** You can drop a
direct image or video URL straight into the script, right after
(or before) the sentence it should illustrate. WideCast (1) strips
the URL (or markdown image construct) from the spoken narration
and (2) uses that asset as the visual for the matching scene,
instead of auto-sourced B-roll. Two equivalent forms — pick by
caller:

  * **Markdown image syntax** (recommended for AI-chat callers
    like Claude / ChatGPT / Grok / Gemini):
    `![brief scene description](https://cdn.acme.com/photo.jpg)`.
    Chat hosts render the picture inline so the end-user can
    visually approve each scene before the script is submitted.
    Alt text doubles as the strongest scene anchor.
  * **Raw URL** on its own line, surrounded by descriptive words
    (the v0.1.0 default; still works):
    `Our cold brew steeps for 16 hours.
    https://cdn.acme.com/coldbrew.jpg That mellow finish…`.

Mix both freely. Supported = direct file links ending in an image
extension (`.png .jpg .jpeg .gif .webp .bmp .avif .svg`) or video
extension (`.mp4 .webm .mov .m4v .avi`), optionally with a
`?query`. Page links (e.g. `https://youtube.com/watch?...`) are
NOT used as inline assets — to turn a whole YouTube/TikTok clip
into a video use `source="video_url"` instead. Keep a few
descriptive words (or alt text) next to the URL so it anchors to
the right scene; multiple URLs are supported; scenes without a
URL still get automatic B-roll.
script_text.example: California parents should encourage their teens to get a driver's license at 16. Driving builds independence, responsibility, and confidence — three things every teenager needs more of, and three things you can't teach from a couch...

idea_text.description:
**Required when `source="idea"`.** Short description of what you
want the video about. The server writes a narration from this
(AI) and continues into the scene-sourcing pipeline. Bounds:
  * minimum 5 words — `idea_too_short` if shorter.
  * maximum 1000 words — longer is auto-truncated at a whitespace
    boundary (NOT rejected). Original word count surfaces in
    `details.input_truncated_from` on `/v1/status`.

Word count = whitespace split.
idea_text.example: Why teens should get their driver's license at 16, not 18 — independence, responsibility, and stake-low practice.

blog_text.description:
**Required when `source="blog"`.** A blog post or article to
repurpose into a video. The server condenses it into a narration
(same AI script-writer as `idea`) then continues into the
scene-sourcing pipeline. Bounds:
  * minimum 30 words — `blog_too_short` if shorter (use
    `source=idea` for a one-liner brief instead).
  * maximum 3000 words — longer is auto-truncated at a whitespace
    boundary (NOT rejected). Original word count surfaces in
    `details.input_truncated_from` on `/v1/status`.

Word count = whitespace split.
blog_text.example: Every hurricane season, thousands of homeowners discover the same painful fact: their homeowner's insurance does not cover flood damage. Standard policies exclude rising-water damage entirely...

video_url.description:
**Required when `source="video_url"`.** A YouTube / TikTok /
Facebook video URL. The server downloads it, then the footage
becomes the B-roll (Auto-Edit). Non-allowed hosts → HTTP 400
`unsupported_media_url`; media over 5 minutes → `media_too_long`.

audio_url.description:
**Required when `source="audio_url"`.** A YouTube / TikTok /
Facebook URL whose audio becomes the narration (Audio-to-Video).
Same host allow-list + 5-minute cap as `video_url`.
**Voice handling**: the user's original voice in the audio is kept
verbatim as the narration in every production_mode (it is never
re-synthesized via TTS). If they pick `production_mode="face_clone"`,
the clone's face is lip-synced TO the user's original audio —
voice stays the user's, only the on-screen face is the clone.

video_file.description:
**Required when `source="video_file"`.** The video file, sent as
multipart/form-data. Caps: **≤ 100 MB** (`file_too_large`) and
**≤ 5 minutes** (`media_too_long`). Only present in the multipart
request variant.

audio_file.description:
**Required when `source="audio_file"`.** The audio file, sent as
multipart/form-data. Caps: **≤ 100 MB** (`file_too_large`) and
**≤ 5 minutes** (`media_too_long`). Only present in the multipart
request variant.

language.description:
**Used when `source="idea"`** (ignored for source=text).
Narration language. v0.1.0 enum locked to English + Vietnamese.
Expanding requires a parity-test bump per A38.

video_length.description:
**Used when `source="idea"`** (ignored for source=text).
Target video length. Maps to legacy `content_type` 9 / 10.
  * `short` — ~90 seconds of narration (content_type 9).
  * `normal` — longer-form, capped at ~3 minutes total
    (content_type 10).

research_enabled.description:
**Used when `source="idea"`** (ignored for source=text).
If true, the AI runs research / fact-check during narration
generation. Default true (matches the UI's default-on behavior).
Disable only if you know your idea is self-contained and
doesn't need external facts.

output_type.description:
How far down the pipeline to run (pipeline depth). For ALL three,
`result.review_url` ships in the create response itself (safe to
share with the user immediately — the page handles early arrival
with an in-page spinner). `video_url` is the field that gates on
completion (output_type=video / after export_video).
  * `text` — stops after the source→script-text phase.
    `review_url` opens the Script Editor.
    ONLY valid for generative sources (source != "text").
    source="text" + output_type="text" → HTTP 400
    `invalid_output_type` (you already supplied the script).
  * `scene` (default) — stops at scenes-ready-for-review.
    `review_url` opens the Scene Editor. Caller can then inspect /
    edit and call `POST /v1/export_video` to render the MP4 — or
    stop there.
  * `video` — auto-chains into the renderer once scenes are ready.
    `result.video_url` populated on completion. Use when you
    trust generated scenes.

faceless.description:
**Used when `output_type` is `scene` or `video`** for sources
text / idea / blog AND for `source=audio_url` — the script comes
from a text input OR from transcribing the user's audio, but the
visuals must still be generated, so the same A/B-roll toggle
applies. When `true`,
EVERY scene is rendered as B-roll (stock video / AI image) with
NO narrator A-roll anywhere — a "faceless" video. When `false`
(default), scenes mix narrator A-roll + B-roll as usual.
Rejected with HTTP 400 `invalid_faceless` when `output_type="text"`
(no scenes are produced) or for video / uploaded-file sources
(`video_url` / `video_file` / `audio_file`).
`production_mode` is the same choice in the skill's words
(`faceless` → true, `face_clone` / `teleprompter` → false); send
either one. The effective value is echoed as `meta.faceless`.

presenter.description:
**AI-presenter ("avatar") lane.** When `true`, the video is rendered with
your AI presenter on screen (the account's photo set; the Video Wizard's
presenter export) instead of the plain A/B-roll render. Omitted or `false` =
today's behaviour exactly.

Requirements, all checked **before any credit is charged**:
* a paid plan (`GET /v1/account` → `features.avatar_video`) — Free / Trial
  accounts get HTTP 402 `plan_required` and can make faceless videos only;
* a ready photo set (`avatar_ready`) — otherwise HTTP 400
  `presenter_not_ready` with `error.details.setup_url` (create the photo set,
  and clone your voice, in WideCast Setup);
* `source` in `text` / `idea` / `blog`, `output_type: "video"`, and not
  combined with `faceless: true` (HTTP 400 `invalid_presenter` otherwise).

The presenter clips are generated while the final video renders, so expect a
longer render than a faceless video, and the presenter export may use
additional credits inside the render (same as the Video Wizard). The newest
usable photo set is used; the response carries it in `meta.presenter.camera_set_id`.

adjust.description:
**Audio sources only** (`audio_url` / `audio_file`) — how the
ingested audio is treated BEFORE the video pipeline (transcription,
scene cutting and all timings run on the treated audio):

* `"off"` (default) — audio used exactly as downloaded/uploaded.
* `"auto"` — run the **autotune** engine: it analyses the speech
  and shapes each phrase's delivery (lifting the lines that carry
  the message, settling the ones that carry weight), then
  normalises speaking pace and loudness. Nothing to configure —
  the engine decides from the content. Best default for raw
  recordings, which are rarely consistent in pace or level.
* `"last_adjust_settings"` — apply the account's saved
  **Adjust Audio** profile (the "Last used" settings from the
  dashboard's Adjust Audio modal: speed / pitch / volume /
  clean up / studio voice). If the account has never saved one,
  behaves like `"off"`.
* An object `{speed?, pitch?, volume?, cleanup?, studio?}` —
  apply exactly this configuration. Omitted keys default to the
  neutral value. `speed` 0.7-1.5 (playback-rate multiple),
  `pitch` integer -5..5 (semitone notches; negative lowers
  the voice, positive raises it), `volume` 0.5-2.0
  (gain multiple; >1.0 soft-clipped), `cleanup` boolean
  (noise / rumble / de-ess), `studio` boolean (compression + EQ).

Treatment failures never fail the request — the original audio
continues (fail-open). Rejected with HTTP 400 `invalid_adjust`
for non-audio sources or out-of-range values.

media_pool.description:
Optional list of **direct image/video file URLs** that aren't placed
inline in the script. WideCast downloads each (image → + thumbnail)
and adds them to the **first scene's** media library, so the scene
editor lists them and the user can drop any into any scene — no
separate media-picker step. Use for images you have but can't
confidently match to a beat (inline the ones you can). Best-effort:
applies on the scene-producing path (text/idea/blog, output_type
scene/video); ignored for output_type='text' / media sources. Same
rule as inline URLs: direct file links only, never fabricated.

wait_for_render.description:
If true, block up to 60s waiting for completion. If the deadline hits
before completion, return the in-flight state and let the client poll.

callback_url.description:
HTTPS URL that will receive a POST when the video completes or fails.
**Accepted but not delivered in pilot — see ROADMAP Phase 1 webhooks.**

metadata.description: Arbitrary key-value pairs stored alongside the video and echoed back on status. Max 16 keys, 500 chars each.

id.description:
`topic_id` returned by `/v1/create_video`. The video must have
reached `scenes_ready_for_review` (HTTP 409 otherwise).

user_confirmed_render.description:
Confirmation flag for AI agents calling via MCP or ChatGPT Action.
**MCP callers**: REQUIRED (the MCP wrapper rejects calls where
this is missing or false). **ChatGPT Action callers**: should set
true after asking the user "Render the final video now, or do
you want to review the scenes first?" and getting an explicit
yes. **SDK / curl / Postman callers**: this field is ignored by
the REST endpoint. Each export is a new decision — never infer
from earlier in the conversation; even if the user wanted the
final video originally, ask again each time.

id.description:
`topic_id` from `/v1/create_video` / `/v1/video_data`. Same id
used by `/v1/status` and `/v1/export_video`. Accepts both
`widecast...` and legacy/current `gubo...`. The video must have
reached `scenes_ready_for_review` (HTTP 409 otherwise).

by.description:
How to pick the scene.
  * `voice_file` — **preferred**. Exact match on the stable
    per-scene UID (also the base of `{voice_file}_spec.json`).
    `segment.id` is only display/order metadata and may change
    after reorder/add/delete.
  * `id` — exact match on the current `segment.id` order/display.
    Use only when you already have it.
  * `text` — fuzzy match against `segment.text`. Multi-match
    returns a 200 `ClarificationResponse` — pass `candidates`
    to the user and re-call with `by="voice_file"`.

value.description: The voice_file / id / narration snippet to match.

fields.description:
Edits to apply. Pick exactly **one family** per call. The only
intentional multi-family call is `layout.batch`, which composes
layout-only children.

**(A) Background media swap** — `mediaUrl` (+ optional
`mediaType`). Roll-aware.

**(B) Upload Overlay** — `remotion.upload_overlay`. Free, agent-
supplied image → Remotion spec (NOT Regenerate, which is paid).

**(C) Remotion object-layer rect** (PREFERRED overlay layout) —
`remotion.object.rect`. Read `boxes.remotion.object_layer.objects`
from `/v1/scene_geometry` first; pass back `{layout_id, x?, y?,
w?, h?, coordinate_space:"preview"|"canvas"}`. Server maps the
rect onto raw Storyboard objects while keeping the group wrapper
unchanged. For `one_by_one`, scene_geometry exposes ONE logical
`*.one_by_one` rect that transforms all timed sequence items
together.

**(D) Remotion group rect** — `remotion.group.rect` (low-level
wrapper edit; prefer (C) for visible overlay layout).
`{element_id?, x?, y?, w?, h?, coordinate_space, resize_mode?}`.

**(E) Narrator layout rect** — `overlay.narrator.rect` (or
field-by-field `overlay.narrator.x|y|w|h`) in 280×498 preview
coords. Preserves narrator metadata + source-space
`segment.narrator_face`.

**(F) Caption Y layout** — `overlay.caption.y` (number) in
280×498 preview coords. Only Y; no text / x / w / h / style.

**(G) Layout batch** — `layout.batch` with
`value:{fields:[...]}` OR multiple layout fields directly.
Allowed children: `overlay.narrator.*`, `overlay.caption.y`,
`remotion.object.rect`, `remotion.group.rect`.

**(H) Upload voice** — `voice.upload` (URL string or `{url,
filename?, content_type?}`); async; queued.

**(I) Upload narrator video** — `narrator.upload_video` (URL
string or `{url, filename?, content_type?}`); async; queued.

**(J) Roll switch** — `roll.active` (`"A"|"B"`) or
`roll.switch` (`"toggle"`); sync data switch.

**(K) Segment text** — `segment.text` (string or `{text}`);
sync, rebuilds word timings from existing audio.

**(L) Scene metadata** — pick from `pattern`, `visual`,
`keyword`, `quote`, `talking_point`, `type`, `sub_mode` (or
`segment.<name>`/`scene.<name>` forms). `pattern`/`type` are
validated against ai_segment_text allow-lists.

**(M) Remotion add element** — `remotion.add_element`. Send
ONE field, append-only. `value = {kind, value?, label?,
url?, position?, rect?, style_token?, emphasis?}` OR a bare
string for `kind="text"`. `kind` ∈ {`text`, `stat`, `label`,
`callout`, `image`}. Returns a new `layout_id` — follow up
with `layout.batch` carrying a matching `remotion.object.rect`
for safe-zone placement.

**(N) Disable overlay** — `disable_overlay` (aliases:
`remotion.disable_overlay`, `overlay.disable`,
`remotion_spec.none`). `value` may be `true`, the string
`"none"`, or `{enabled:false}`. Sets
`segment.remotion_spec="none"` without deleting the
`{voice_file}_spec.json` / overlay-poster files. Must be
sent ALONE. Re-enable later via (B) Upload Overlay.

value.description:
Family-dependent. URL string for `mediaUrl` /
`remotion.upload_overlay` / `voice.upload` /
`narrator.upload_video`. `"image"`|`"video"` for
`mediaType`. Object `{layout_id, x?, y?, w?, h?,
coordinate_space}` for `remotion.object.rect`. Object
`{element_id?, x?, y?, w?, h?, coordinate_space,
resize_mode?}` for `remotion.group.rect`. Object
`{x, y, w, h, visible?, animation?, borderRadius?}` for
`overlay.narrator.rect`. Number for individual narrator
axes and `overlay.caption.y`. Object `{fields:[...]}`
for `layout.batch`. `"A"`|`"B"` for `roll.active`,
`"toggle"` for `roll.switch`. String for `segment.text`
and metadata fields. Object `{kind, value?, label?,
url?, position?, rect?, style_token?, emphasis?,
entry?, delay_sec?, z_index?, element_z_index?}` (or
bare string for kind=text) for `remotion.add_element`.

min_score.description:
Only when `by="text"`. Acceptance threshold for fuzzy match.
Lower cautiously for paraphrases; raising past 0.9 usually
causes false negatives because exact text rarely matches
verbatim.

ModifySceneRequest.description:
Body for POST /v1/modify_scene. SYNCHRONOUS, no credit charged. On
ambiguous text match the response is a 200 `ClarificationResponse`
— no edit applied, retry with `by="voice_file"`. Successful edits
publish MQTT realtime to every open editor for this video.

SceneCandidate.description:
One ambiguous-match candidate returned when `by="text"` could not
decide between two or more scenes. Use `voice_file` (preferred) or
`segment_id` to call /v1/modify_scene again with `by="voice_file"`.

text.description: First ~80 chars of the scene's narration (preview).

SceneModifiedResponse.description:
Success body for POST /v1/modify_scene. Shape varies slightly
across the three edit families (media / upload_overlay /
group_rect); fields not relevant to the family are omitted.

skill_required.description: Backup signal — see SkillRequiredHint. Tells the agent to load the editing skill BEFORE continuing.

scene_id.description: segment.id of the scene that was edited (current display/order only — voice_file is the stable id).

voice_file.description: Stable per-scene UID of the edited scene.

score.description:
Resolution confidence (1.0 for `by="id"`/`by="voice_file"`; fuzzy
score for `by="text"`).

applied.description:
Which family of edits ran + family-specific details. Older
media-only responses carried a string (`"media"`); current
responses carry an object with `cost`, `uploaded_overlay_url`,
or `group_rect_summary` depending on the family.

media_type.description: Set when the background media branch ran. Resolved asset type.

media_url.description: Set when the background media branch ran. The URL agent supplied.

segment.description:
The full updated segment as stored after the edit (deep-copy,
so caller can compare before/after). Includes `mediaUrl`,
`brollUrl`, `overlay.*`, `remotion_spec`, etc. — same shape as
entries in `/v1/video_data.segments`.

remotion_spec_updated.description: True when the edit produced a new `{voice_file}_spec.json` (overlay upload / group rect).

remotion_spec_url.description: Cache-busted public spec URL (`?v=<mtime>`); empty when state ≠ ready.

uploaded_overlay_url.description: Set on the Upload Overlay branch (the image URL the agent supplied).

cost.description: Set on the Upload Overlay branch — always 0 (free path).

layout_batch_updated.description: True when the call ran the `layout.batch` composer.

narrator_layout_updated.description: True when a narrator rect / axis edit was applied (single-field or as a layout.batch child).

caption_layout_updated.description: True when an `overlay.caption.y` edit was applied (single-field or as a layout.batch child).

remotion_object_updated.description: True when `remotion.object.rect` was applied (single-field or as a layout.batch child).

remotion_element_added.description:
True when the (M) `remotion.add_element` branch ran. The
`applied` object on this branch carries the new
`element_id`, `object_id`, `layout_id` (= `{element_id}.{object_id}`),
`rect` (280×498 preview), `rect_canvas` (720×1280),
`auto_fit: false`, `cost: "free_spec_append"`, and a
`follow_up` hint pointing at the recommended
`layout.batch` + `remotion.object.rect` placement step.

overlay_disabled.description:
True when the (N) `disable_overlay` branch ran —
`segment.remotion_spec` was set to `"none"` (no
`{voice_file}_spec.json` / overlay-poster files deleted).
The `applied` object on this branch carries `before` (the
prior `remotion_spec` value), `after: "none"`, and
`idempotent: true` when the scene was already disabled.

remotion_poster_file.description: Canonical `{voice_file}_overlay_poster.png` — derived static overlay poster used by server-side scene_inspector screenshot fallback.

remotion_poster_url.description: Cache-busted public poster URL (`?v=<mtime>`); empty when state ≠ ready.

remotion_poster_warnings.description: Warnings emitted while rendering the static overlay poster (e.g. missing assets).

active_roll.description: Set on the A/B-roll branch — the new active roll (`"A"` or `"B"`).

show_narrator.description: Set on the A/B-roll branch — whether the narrator is shown after the switch.

SceneUploadQueuedResponse.description:
Async queued response for the `voice.upload` and
`narrator.upload_video` branches of `/v1/modify_scene`. The edit is
not yet visible — wait for MQTT
`scene_voice_upload_applied` /
`scene_narrator_upload_applied`, then call `/v1/video_data` to
verify.

queue_id.description: e.g. `gs_{topic_id}_{voice_file}` — share with the worker via MQTT.

segment.description: Snapshot of the resolved segment at queue time.

SceneGeometryRequest.description:
Body for POST /v1/scene_geometry. Provide exactly one of:
  - `voice_file` (preferred shortcut),
  - `scene_id` (display/order; fallback),
  - or `by` + `value`.
When neither shortcut is set and `by` is omitted, the request is
rejected with `invalid_by`.

id.description:
Topic id from `/v1/video_data` / `/v1/create_video`. Accepts
`widecast...`, `gubo...`, or current ids.

by.description:
How to pick the scene. Prefer `voice_file`. Use `text` only
when the user names a scene by narration; multi-match returns
a `ClarificationResponse`.

value.description: The id / voice_file / narration snippet to inspect.

voice_file.description: Stable per-scene UID — preferred shortcut (server folds into `by="voice_file"`).

include_diagnostics.description:
Optional debug flag. When `true`, the response also carries
`violations[]`, `warnings[]`, `summary.error_count` /
`summary.warning_count`, and the `remotion_poster_*` keys
inside `remotion_spec`. Default is `false` because mechanical
linter output is debug-only — vision-capable agents should
judge aesthetics from a screenshot via `/v1/scene_inspector`,
and LLM-only agents should proceed with the rects +
`boxes.narrator.face` to keep overlays out of the face.

SceneGeometryResponse.description:
Data-only scene layout geometry. Every box is in
**280×498 editor-preview** coordinates unless explicitly suffixed
with `_canvas` (Remotion 720×1280 canvas).

**Mechanical linter output is stripped by default.** `violations`,
`warnings`, `summary.error_count`, and `summary.warning_count`
are only present when the request included
`include_diagnostics: true`.

skill_required.description: Backup signal — see SkillRequiredHint. Tells the agent to load the editing skill BEFORE continuing.

narrator.description:
`{rect, visible, face_source, face, face_center,
face_coordinate_space_note}`. `face` is the displayed face
box — converted from source-space `segment.narrator_face`
through the current `overlay.narrator.rect`. Do NOT mutate
`segment.narrator_face` for layout edits.

caption.description:
`{container_rect, text_rect_estimate, visible}`. Read-only
for layout decisions; only `overlay.caption.y` is mutable.

remotion.description:
Remotion Storyboard boxes.
  - `object_layer.objects[]` is the **agent-facing**
    layer: each item has `layout_id`, `rect`,
    `rect_canvas`, `temporal_policy`, and the update
    field name to pass back to `/v1/modify_scene`
    (`remotion.object.rect`).
  - `groups[]`, `objects[]`, `sequence_objects[]` are
    lower-level debug data.

remotion_spec.description:
Metadata for the loaded `{voice_file}_spec.json` —
file/url/version/state. The internal `remotion_poster_*`
keys (file, url, version, state, exists, warnings) are
stripped by default; pass `include_diagnostics: true` to
surface them.

violations.description:
**Diagnostic only — present only when
`include_diagnostics=true`.** Collision codes (error /
warning / info severity) such as
`remotion_object_overlaps_narrator_face`,
`remotion_object_in_top_dead_zone`,
`remotion_group_in_bottom_dead_zone`,
`caption_text_overlaps_narrator_face`. Vision-capable
agents should judge collisions from a screenshot instead.

warnings.description:
**Diagnostic only — present only when
`include_diagnostics=true`.** Soft signals such as
`remotion_object_too_small_for_mobile`,
`narrator_face_outside_narrator`, `missing_narrator_face`.

AssetResponse.description:
Success body for POST /v1/upload_asset (multipart or JSON+base64). The
`url` is publicly reachable (S3 anonymous-read), valid for **24
hours** before the bucket lifecycle rule on the `assets/` prefix
deletes the object.

url.description: Public S3 URL — pass into /v1/create_video as audio_url / video_url, or use as an inline `![](url)` in script_text.

content_type.description: The Content-Type the object was stored with (may differ from the request if defaulted from the extension).

filename.description: Original basename of the upload (≤128 chars). For tracking only; not part of the URL path.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when the bucket lifecycle rule will delete the object.

ttl_hours.description: TTL relative to upload time, in hours.

AssetPresignRequest.description:
Request body for POST /v1/upload_asset with `mode: "presign"` — the
path AI agents take (MCP can't carry binary). Server mints an S3 PUT
URL the caller uses directly. No bytes through this call.

filename.description: Original filename — used to pick the S3 extension (`.mp4`, `.mp3`, `.png`, …). Basename only; any path is stripped.

content_type.description: Optional MIME type. Used by the downstream pipeline only (informational) — NOT bound to the S3 signature, so the caller does NOT need to echo it back on the PUT.

AssetUploadJSONRequest.description:
Legacy / small-file JSON body — bytes inline as base64. Server cap
500 MB decoded; the MCP transport caps you to ~25 MB per call, so
agents take the `AssetPresignRequest` path instead.

file_data.description: Raw asset bytes, **base64-encoded**. No `data:...;base64,` prefix needed (silently stripped).

filename.description: Original filename — used to pick the on-disk extension (`.mp4`, `.mp3`, `.png`, …).

content_type.description: Optional MIME type (e.g. `audio/mpeg`, `video/mp4`, `image/jpeg`, `text/html`, `application/pdf`, `text/markdown`). Falls back to detection from the filename extension if omitted.

AssetPresignResponse.description:
Success body for POST /v1/upload_asset with `mode: "presign"`. The
caller PUTs the asset bytes to `put_url` (must echo back the
`headers_required` Content-Type), then uses `get_url` as their public
URL. `put_url` is valid for 1 hour; `get_url` resolves for 24 hours
after the PUT lands (bucket lifecycle).

put_url.description: Pre-signed S3 PUT URL. PUT your bytes here with the headers in `headers_required`. Valid for 1 hour.

get_url.description: Public S3 URL — pass into /v1/create_video as audio_url / video_url, or use as an inline `![](url)` in script_text.

headers_required.description:
Headers the caller MUST add to the PUT. Empty by design — the
signature only binds `host`, so `curl -X PUT --upload-file <file>
"<put_url>"` (no extra headers) works as-is across HTTP clients.

max_bytes.description: Hard server cap on the PUT body size, in bytes.

put_expires_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when `put_url` stops being accepted.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when the bucket lifecycle rule will delete the object.

ttl_hours.description: TTL relative to upload time, in hours.

NotificationSendRequest.description:
Body for `POST /v1/notification/send`. The recipient (email address
+ Telegram chat) is resolved server-side from the API key's account
— there is no `to` / `chat_id` field by design (prevents using
WideCast as a notification spam relay).

subject.description:
REQUIRED. The email subject line; also prepended in **bold**
before the Telegram message body. Keep it short (≤200 bytes) —
the server returns `subject_too_long` (400) beyond that.

message.description:
The notification body (email body / Telegram text), OR the
caption when `photo_url` / `video_url` is set. Telegram caps
captions at 1024 bytes — the server pre-validates and returns
`message_too_long` (400) if you exceed that in caption mode.

parse_mode.description:
Optional Telegram formatting mode for the body. Omit for plain
text. `HTML` supports a small tag subset (b, i, u, s, code, pre,
a); the server strips other tags. The subject is always bolded
automatically.

photo_url.description:
Optional photo to attach. Public http(s) URL — Telegram
downloads it; email embeds it inline. Mutually exclusive with
`video_url`.

video_url.description:
Optional video to attach. Public http(s) URL — Telegram
downloads it; email shows a clickable link. Mutually exclusive
with `photo_url`.

ErrorReportRequest.description:
Body for `POST /v1/error/report`. The reporting account (company +
email) is resolved server-side from the API key — there is no
company/user field by design.

error_message.description:
REQUIRED. What went wrong. Prefer the verbatim error text the
failing call returned over a paraphrase.

module.description:
Which part of WideCast failed, e.g. `export`, `scene_upload`,
`spec`, `modify_scene`, `video_data`. Free-form — it only groups
reports for triage. Defaults to `agent` for API callers.

context.description:
Free-form debugging details — `topic_id`, `voice_file`,
`scene_id`, what you were attempting, and above all the
`request_id` of the failing call when you have one. At most 50
keys are rendered into the report.

reported.description: Always `true` on a 200 — the report reached the WideCast team.

module.description: The module the report was filed under (after defaulting/truncation).

context_keys.description: How many `context` keys were included in the report.

page_url.description: The page the owner was on.

TicketCreateRequest.description:
`title` plus `actual` or `error` are required; every other field helps the team find
the problem faster. Never put a key, a password or a cookie in any field.

title.description: One line that names the problem.

expected.description: What the owner asked for or expected.

boss_words.description: The owner's own words about it, as they said them.

error.description: The error text exactly as shown.

command.description: The command or call that failed.

runtime.description: Runtime class: LOCAL, REMOTE or HOSTED.

platform.description: The agent and platform, e.g. `Meta Muse`.

client.description: The client slug the problem is about.

node.description: The node name of this install.

duplicate.description: `true`: the same problem already had an open ticket, which now counts this one.

context.description: The report's context, on an `auto` ticket.

release_id.description: The WideCast release you run now.

NotificationResponse.description:
Success body for POST /v1/notification/send. `delivery` lists the
channels that were delivered successfully; per-channel `email` /
`telegram` objects carry each channel's own status.

status.description: `sent` = every attempted channel succeeded; `partial` = at least one but not all succeeded.

delivery.description: The channels that were delivered successfully.

reason.description: Set when status=skipped (e.g. subject+body over Telegram's byte limit).

note.description: Set when delivered via Telegram only (no email on file).

ClientLinkSendRequest.description:
Body for `POST /v1/client_link/send`. Recipients are ALWAYS
resolved server-side from the account's Setup > Notification
settings — there is no phone/email field by design (prevents using
WideCast as a notification spam relay).

ttl_days.description: Link lifetime in days. Out-of-range values are clamped to 1..30.

channels.description:
Which of the account's notification channels deliver the link.
Omitted, empty, or all-false => MINT-ONLY (no notification is
sent; the caller gets `magic_url` and decides later).

telegram.description: Send via the account's connected Telegram chat.

sms.description: Send via SMS (Twilio) to the account's configured phone number.

email.description: Send via email to the account's configured address.

page.description: Which app page hosts the link.

ClientLinkResponse.description:
Success body for POST /v1/client_link/send. `results` is present
only when channels were requested; per-channel objects carry their
own status.

magic_url.description: The no-login client link. Hand it to the client or send it later.

expires_in_days.description: The applied link lifetime (after clamping), in days.

notified.description: `true` when at least one notification channel delivered the link.

results.description:
Present only when channels were requested. Per-channel delivery
status: `sent` | `skipped` | `failed` (with `reason` / `error`).

content.description:
What the content is created from: a URL, an idea/topic description,
or pasted text.

content_type.description:
What to write: `blog` (long-form), `facebook`, `x` (Twitter/X), or
`linkedin` post. Maps to the legacy content_type 3/4/5/6 internally.

callback_url.description: Optional HTTPS webhook for completion events.

metadata.description: Optional key-value pairs echoed back on /v1/status.

CreateContentRequest.description:
Body for POST /v1/create_content. Async — returns a widecast* id +
`result.review_url` (the content viewer) in the create response itself
(share immediately; viewer shows a spinner). Poll GET /v1/status/{id}
until `completed` for the final state.

CreateImageRequest.description:
Body for POST /v1/create_image. Charges 1 credit per image
generated (count=4 → 4 credits).

prompt.description:
Image description. Concrete visual nouns work better than
abstract concepts — "a wooden ladder against a red brick wall,
morning light" beats "climbing the corporate ladder".

purpose.description:
What the image is for. `scene` (default) = today's behaviour: a video
background / scene image (video orientation, text kept inside the video safe
zone). `social` = a standalone post image: the requested `ratio` is honoured
exactly (centre-cropped when the engine returns a near size) and NO video
safe-zone instruction is added to the prompt.

ratio.description:
Output aspect ratio. With `purpose: scene` (default): `portrait`=768×1344
(Reels/TikTok/Shorts), `landscape`=1344×768 (YouTube/blog hero),
`square`=768×768 (IG feed). With `purpose: social`: one of `1:1`, `4:5`,
`16:9`, `9:16` (default `1:1`; the words portrait / landscape / square are
accepted as aliases for 9:16 / 16:9 / 1:1). A ratio from the wrong family
is rejected with HTTP 400 `invalid_ratio`.

count.description:
How many variations to generate in one call. Each = 1 credit.
Use `count=3..4` when the user wants options to pick from.

topic_id.description:
Optional. Link the generated image to an existing video's asset
folder so the scene editor can reuse it. Omit for freeform.

number.description: 1-based index — agents render a numbered thumbnail list keyed off this.

url.description: Public URL to the full-resolution image asset.

thumbnail_url.description: URL to use as the thumbnail (currently same as `url`).

status.description:
`completed` if every requested variant succeeded; `partial` if
some variants failed (see `error` + the surviving `images`).

purpose.description: Echoed only when the request used purpose=social.

agent_note.description:
Short instruction for AI agents: record the image(s) in the local dashboard
library (see `result.library_record`). Present on `completed` responses.

TypographyRequest.description: Body for POST /v1/typography. 1 credit per call.

role.description:
`typography` = a key phrase mid-video (template typography, word by
word or line by line). `opening_poster` = the opening hook poster.
`cta_poster` = the closing call-to-action poster. Posters are
UPPERCASE, at most 3 lines of 4 words.

text.description: The narration of this moment (context for the engines).

quote.description:
The words to set. `|` (also `->`, `→`, a new line) is a hard line
break. Typography defaults to `text`; posters write their own copy
from `text` unless `exact` is true.

language.description: Language code, e.g. vi, en. Default vi.

words.description: Word timings of the narration, seconds from the start of this moment. Optional context for the engine's choice of layout (word by word or line by line).

duration.description: Seconds this moment lasts. Default: from words.

show_narrator.description: A narrator is on screen: posters keep to the lower band, clear of the face.

exact.description: Posters: use quote exactly as written ('|' lines kept).

brand.description: The brand's colours, main first. Pulls the engines' own palettes toward them.

cta.description: Contact line for a cta_poster (else the account's profile is used).

look.description: One id per video: calls with the same look share one style.

wait.description: Seconds to wait for the result.

TypographyObject.description: One object of the design, listed in paint order (back to front).

name.description: The engine's object id (e.g. p0_line2, p0_line2w1 for a word, p0_deco1).

text.description: The text this object shows (null for decorations).

svg_url.description: Self-contained SVG of the object: text converted to outlines (no font needed), sized to its box, vector. Null only when the engine produced no SVG (then use image_url).

image_url.description: Transparent PNG of the object at twice the canvas scale (box.w×2 by box.h×2 pixels).

box.description: Where WideCast places it on the canvas (720×1280). Draw the SVG or PNG at this box.

phase.description: Present when the design has several phases (p0_, p1_ …) that replace each other over time.

lines.description: The phrase split at its line breaks.

preview_url.description: PNG of the whole set as WideCast places it, on the transparent canvas: look at it before placing the objects.

brand.description: What the brand colours were mapped to.

keyword.description:
Search keyword (1-3 words work best). Pexels/Pixabay token-match
poorly with sentence-long queries — keep it tight.

kind.description:
What to search: `video` = stock CLIPS (Pexels/Pixabay/Shutterstock,
broll.js Stock tab); `image` = real PHOTOS (Google, broll.js
Photos tab).

ratio.description:
Orientation hint. Only filters when `kind == "video"`. Image
search ignores it (crop client-side if needed).

number.description: 1-based index — agents render a numbered thumbnail list keyed off this.

url.description: Public URL to the full-resolution asset.

context_url.description: Web page the image was crawled from (image results only).

VideoDataSegmentNarrator.description:
Narrator block on a scene segment (face/voice clone or recorded
media). All fields optional — populated only when the scene has a
narrator configured (A-roll, or B-roll that opted-in to voiceover).

VideoDataSegment.description:
One annotated scene/segment in the video_data response. Includes
stable-identity fields and Remotion spec metadata for agent
editing.

id.description:
Current display/order id. UNSTABLE — may change after
reorder/add/delete. Use `voice_file` as the stable scene UID.

voice_file.description:
Stable per-scene UID. Pass as `value` with `by="voice_file"` to
`/v1/modify_scene`. Also the base of the Remotion spec filename
`{voice_file}_spec.json`.

scene_index.description: 0-based index into the segments array (current order).

text.description: Narration (what the narrator says on this scene).

visual.description: Visual-direction hint (what the scene's visual should convey).

quote.description: Pull-quote (when the scene type uses one).

keyword.description: Single-word search keyword used for stock B-roll fallback.

type.description: Scene role — `A-roll` (narrator on screen), `B-roll` (background only), `thumbnail`, or empty.

mediaUrl.description: Currently-shown background or A-roll overlay asset URL.

brollUrl.description: Pure B-roll URL (may differ from `mediaUrl` when an A-roll overlay was added).

videoTrim.description: `{start, end}` trim values when the scene uses a video clip.

overlay.description:
Legacy overlay block — `caption` + `narrator` rects in **280×498**
editor preview coordinates. Distinct from the Remotion spec
(which uses 720×1280 canvas coords).

remotion_spec.description:
Per-scene Remotion spec filename token (or `null`). `"none"`
means the user intentionally disabled the overlay for that
scene — agents must NOT auto-edit or re-enable unless the user
asks.

remotion_spec_url.description:
Cache-busted public URL
`https://widecast.ai/downloads/{company_id}/{topic_id}/{voice_file}_spec.json?v={mtime}`.
Empty when state is `missing` or `disabled`.

remotion_poster_file.description:
**Diagnostic only — present only when
`include_diagnostics=true`.** Canonical
`{voice_file}_overlay_poster.png` — derived static overlay
poster used by server-side scene_inspector screenshot
fallback.

remotion_poster_url.description: **Diagnostic only — present only when `include_diagnostics=true`.** Cache-busted public poster URL (`?v=<mtime>`).

remotion_poster_warnings.description: **Diagnostic only — present only when `include_diagnostics=true`.** Warnings emitted while rendering the static overlay poster.

agent_meta.description:
Same metadata bundled for quick consumption:
`stable_scene_id_field="voice_file"`, `stable_scene_id`,
`order_field="id"`, `order_value`, `scene_index`,
`remotion_spec` (same metadata; the inner `remotion_poster_*`
keys are diagnostic-only — only present when
`include_diagnostics=true`), `coordinate_spaces` (the
720×1280 canvas + 280×498 preview maps).

VideoDataGlobalSettings.description:
Slim subset of the script's globalSettings — only user-facing
fields surfaced (deeply nested render-only knobs are not in this
public response). Currently: `aspectRatio`, `voice_type`,
`avatar_type`, `last_voice_type`, `last_avatar_type`.

SceneIdentityGuide.description: Machine-readable scene-identity rules embedded in /v1/video_data responses.

SkillRequiredHint.description:
Backup signal stamped on every successful JSON response from the 4
edit-flow endpoints (`/v1/video_data`, `/v1/scene_geometry`,
`/v1/scene_inspector`, `/v1/modify_scene`). Tells the agent: "you
reached this endpoint without first loading the editing skill — do
so now." Skip it only if you have ALREADY loaded
`GET /v1/skills/editing` earlier in the session. Idempotent;
emitting on every call is cheap, and the agent learns once.

load_via_tool.description: MCP tool name to call (when running via MCP).

load_via_rest.description: REST endpoint to call (when running via HTTP/SDK).

VideoDataResponse.description:
**URL-RESPONSE ENVELOPE.** Default delivery mode is
`download_url`: the server publishes the full video_data tree to
a temporary public JSON file on `origin.widecast.ai` and the
response carries `data.url` + size + 15-min TTL + a 3-step
`instructions` block. The agent must `curl <data.url> -o
video_data.json` and Read locally; the full tree is NOT inlined
in this response. This bypasses MCP per-tool-call output caps
that previously truncated 50–300 KB payloads mid-JSON. Every
call publishes a NEW unique file (token = 16 hex chars) so URLs
are never reused — matches the realtime semantics of video
data. Host is `origin.widecast.ai` (CF-bypassed) +
`?v=<mtime>` cache-bust. Server only responds AFTER the JSON is
fsynced + atomically renamed, so the URL is guaranteed
readable. The published JSON file shape is unchanged: top-level
`object`/`id`/`topic_id`/`aspect_ratio`/`title`/`language`/
`total_segments`/`total_duration`/`scene_identity`/`segments[]`/
`global_settings`/`review_url`/`request_id`. Operators can flip
to legacy inline mode with env flag
`WIDECAST_VIDEO_DATA_DELIVERY_MODE=inline_content`.

skill_required.description: Backup signal — see SkillRequiredHint. Tells the agent to load the editing skill BEFORE continuing.

delivery_mode.description:
`download_url` (default) → `data` carries a URL pointer; agent fetches the JSON file.
`inline_content` → legacy mode (set via env flag); the full video_data tree is inlined.

data.description: Pointer to the published JSON file. Set when `delivery_mode="download_url"`.

expires_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp — ~15 min after publish.

instructions.description: 3-step setup the agent should follow (mkdir + curl + Read).

review_url.description: Scene-editor URL — opens this video in the dashboard's editor for review/edit.

id.description: Topic id from `/v1/video_data` / scene_editor. Accepts widecast..., gubo..., or current topic ids.

action.description:
Inspector action. Prefer `get_computed_boxes` /
`get_scene_dom_snapshot` for structural audit. Use
`screenshot_scene_280x498` for the composite scene visual
(background + Remotion overlay poster + narrator +
caption). Use `overlay_poster` to audit ONLY the overlay
on a solid black canvas — the composite screenshot can
hide readability / typos / grammar / diacritic / glyph
issues that the background image masks. Both actions
return a 15-minute public JPEG URL and are pure
server-side compositors.

scene_id.description: Current display/order scene id. Prefer `voice_file` when available.

voice_file.description: Stable per-scene UID from `/v1/video_data`; preferred selector.

selector.description: Optional DOM selector scoped to the target preview root (used by `get_scene_dom_snapshot` / `get_computed_boxes`). Avoid broad selectors.

activate.description: Allow the elected browser to activate/load the requested scene before inspecting. May visibly switch the open editor scene for that user.

seek_seconds.description: Optional seek time for `seek_preview` or screenshot capture.

SceneInspectorResponse.description:
Outcome of a live inspector call. `status` discriminates the
downstream branches an agent should take.

skill_required.description: Backup signal — see SkillRequiredHint. Tells the agent to load the editing skill BEFORE continuing.

code.description:
`ok` | `no_live_editor` | `no_active_editor` |
`unsupported_action` | `publisher_missing` |
`mqtt_publish_failed` | `browser_error` |
`screenshot_publish_failed` (composed but couldn't be
persisted to disk — HTTP 500) | `overlay_not_available`
(scene has no Remotion overlay poster — HTTP 409) |
`overlay_publish_failed` (overlay JPEG couldn't be
persisted — HTTP 500). Successful `screenshot_scene_280x498`
calls return this JSON envelope with `code: "ok"` and
`result.screenshot.url`; successful `overlay_poster` calls
return `code: "ok"` and `result.overlay_poster.url` plus
`result.review_checklist`. Both actions are pure
server-side compositors — successful compose is always
`code: "ok"` regardless of live-editor presence.

selected_browser.description: Tab metadata for the elected browser (set only when `status="completed"`).

result.description: Action-specific result payload from the elected browser.

product_service_input.description: Describe the product/service to brainstorm ideas from (≥ 10 chars).
product_service_input.example: A budgeting app for freelancers with tax estimates

user_location.description:
Where the user is based (city/state/country). Used as a hint; can
differ from `target_location` (a Vietnam-based agency may target
a US audience).

target_location.description:
**Required (semantically).** Audience market the videos should
target (city/state/country). Drives which local trends, sources,
and language are used. If you call without this AND the account
doesn't have one cached, the API returns **HTTP 200** with
`{object: "clarification", needs_input: "target_location", message: …}`
and DOES NOT charge a credit — relay the message to the user,
get their answer, then retry. Do NOT infer from chat context —
ask explicitly; the target market can differ from where the user
is based.

CollectIdeasRequest.description: Body for POST /v1/collect_ideas (synchronous → IdeasResponse OR Clarification).

AddToProductionPlanRequest.description:
Body for `POST /v1/production_plan/add`. The account is resolved
server-side from the API key — there is no company/user field.

idea_text.description: REQUIRED. The idea / topic line to queue into the production plan.

description.description: Optional longer description / notes for the idea.

industry.description: Optional industry tag. Falls back to the account's saved industry when omitted.

source.description:
Optional provenance tag (default `idea`). Use `template`
together with `template` to start the entry in the `ab_roll`
workflow phase instead of `queued`.

week_start.description: Optional unix timestamp (seconds) for the plan week; used as the entry's creation_time. Defaults to now.

topic_id.description: Optional stable id for the entry: 8-128 characters of letters, digits, `_` or `-`, starting with a letter or digit (else 400 `invalid_topic_id`). Auto-generated (`widecast<hex>`) when omitted.

template.description: Advanced: template id when queuing from a foundation template (source='template').

core_topics.description: Advanced: core topics for the idea.

short_headline.description: Advanced: a short headline for the entry.

recommended.description:
Optional. Set `true` to flag this idea as your recommended pick —
useful when an agent adds several generated ideas and wants to
highlight one. The dashboard's plan list shows a **Recommended**
badge on the entry (top-right). Idea-level flag — NOT the same as
`recommended_format`, which picks the master script version.

scripts.description:
Optional — **script attach**. 1-5 pre-written script versions,
one per format (formats must be unique). When sent, the idea is
stored already "Script ready" (no LLM call, no credit): opening
it in the dashboard goes straight into the Script Editor with
the supplied version(s) selectable in the 5-format strip. The
recommended version becomes the master script; the others land
as ready versions. Do not combine with a `topic_id` that
already has a video/script (409 `topic_exists`).

format.description: Script angle: VE=Value Explainer, QA=Client Q&A, POV, CS=Case Study, MB=Myth-Buster.

text.description: Full script text for this format — 80-1000 words.

language.description:
Optional. Language of the attached scripts (e.g. `English`,
`Vietnamese`). Defaults to the account's saved output language.

topic_id.description: The queued entry's id (generated if the caller didn't pass one).

scripts_attached.description:
Present only when `scripts` was sent — the formats stored, in
the fixed VE→QA→POV→CS→MB order.

recommended_format.description: Present only when `scripts` was sent — the master format.

script_ready.description:
Present (`true`) only when `scripts` was sent — the idea already
carries its script(s); opening it skips the writing step.

ClarificationResponse.description:
Returned by endpoints that need an additional input from the user
before they can produce a result. The server returns HTTP 200 (NOT
an error) so AI agents can relay the prompt without surfacing it as
a failure. No credits are charged for this response. The endpoint
is safe to retry as soon as the named field is provided.

Currently emitted by:
  * POST /v1/collect_ideas — when `target_location` is missing AND
    the account has no cached target market.
  * POST /v1/modify_scene — when `by="text"` matches two or more
    scenes too closely; `candidates` carries the list to disambiguate
    with the user.

needs_input.description:
Name of the missing input field — match it against the request
schema. Set the value the user provides on this field and retry
the same endpoint.

message.description:
Prompt to relay to the user (in their language if appropriate).
Already explains what the field is, why it matters, and what
format to expect.
message.example: Which target market / audience location should these video ideas target? e.g. 'California, United States', 'Texas, US', or 'Vietnam'.

candidates.description:
Only set by /v1/modify_scene when `by="text"` is ambiguous. List
of scenes that matched the supplied text closely enough to be
plausible. Show the `text` previews to the user, then call
/v1/modify_scene again with `by="voice_file"` and the chosen
scene's `voice_file`.

PublishRequest.description:
Body for POST /v1/publish. Provide EXACTLY ONE of `topic_id`, `text`,
or `video_url`.

topic_id.description:
Publish an existing WideCast video OR blog/social post (the id from
/v1/create_video or /v1/create_content). Article vs video is
auto-detected.

text.description: Arbitrary text to post (optionally with photo_urls).

video_url.description: A direct video file URL (mp4/mov/…) to download + publish. Requires `title`.

title.description: Caption/title. Required when `video_url` is given; optional override for `topic_id`.

platforms.description: Target platforms. Defaults to ALL connected platforms of the chosen channel group.

channel_group.description:
Channel group to publish through (0 = primary, default). A channel
group is a separate set of connected accounts (e.g. English vs
Vietnamese channels); one call publishes through ONE group. List
groups with GET /v1/channel_groups.

scheduled_date.description: Optional ISO date/time to schedule the post (with `timezone`).

platform_settings.description:
Per-call overrides `{platform: {key: value}}`, merged over the saved
settings of the chosen channel group for THIS post only — the saved
settings are not changed. Use it to pick the post type / page / privacy
for one post. Facebook keys: `facebook_media_type` = `REELS` (default;
Facebook trims long videos to ~90 s) | `VIDEO` (long-form video post) |
`STORIES`; `facebook_page_id`; `facebook_video_state` = `Published` |
`Draft`. Instagram: `media_type` = `REELS` | `STORIES`. YouTube:
`privacyStatus` = `public` | `unlisted` | `private`.

ChannelGroup.description:
One CHANNEL GROUP — a separate set of connected social accounts backed
by its own publishing profile (e.g. "Vietnamese channels" vs "English
channels"). Group 0 is the primary group and always exists; every
endpoint that takes `channel_group` defaults to 0.

channel_group.description: Stable group number. 0 = primary. Numbers are never reused after removal.

created_at.description: Unix seconds (0 for the primary group).

ShortLink.description:
A short link https://widecast.ai/s/<id> that redirects (302) to `url`.
Belongs to one account; the ID never changes.

id.description: The part after widecast.ai/s/. New IDs are upper-case.

short_url.description: The link to share, exactly as returned.

clicks.description: How many times the link was opened (includes opens not yet saved).

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC of the last destination change; null if never changed.

url.description: REQUIRED. The long link to shorten. Must be a full http:// or https:// URL (no spaces, no user:password). SDK constant `SHORT_LINK_URL_MAX_CHARS`.

custom_id.description:
Optional. The ID after widecast.ai/s/: 4-32 letters or digits only
(no spaces, dashes or other symbols), case-insensitive and stored in
capitals. Omit it for a random 6-character ID without 0 and O.
SDK constants `SHORT_LINK_CUSTOM_ID_MIN_CHARS` / `SHORT_LINK_CUSTOM_ID_MAX_CHARS`.

url.description: REQUIRED. The new destination: a full http:// or https:// URL. SDK constant `SHORT_LINK_URL_MAX_CHARS`.

PublishResponse.description:
Accepted-publish envelope (HTTP 202). Poll GET /v1/status/{id} with any
of `request_ids` for per-platform results.

request_ids.description: All upstream request_ids (an article spanning text+photo may return two).

platforms.description: Platforms the publish was dispatched to.

skipped.description: Platforms skipped (not connected / missing required config).

channel_group.description: Channel group the post was dispatched through (0 = primary).

topic_id.description: The WideCast video / article that was published. Present only when the request used `topic_id`.

content_kind.description:
What was published: `video` (a WideCast video or an external `video_url`),
`article` (a WideCast blog / social text), `text`, or `photo` (`text` + `photo_urls`).

agent_note.description:
Short instruction for AI agents: poll the status id, then record the post in the
local dashboard library (`<bridge> tool provider call --operation getStatus --path id=<id>`
files it; or pass the status response's `result.library_record` to
`<bridge> tool content import --json`). Ignore it if you keep no local dashboard.

Status.description: Unified async-task status envelope returned by `create_video` and `get_status`.

topic_id.description:
Mirrors `id` 1:1. Exposed separately because the legacy `/checkProgress`
response and the scene-editor URL (`?topic_id=`) use this name —
clients can pick whichever field name reads more clearly.

type.description:
Resource type. `video` for create_video / enhance_script ids;
`content` for create_content (written blog/social — `details.status`
carries the blog_status stage: Queued / Processing / Researching /
Deep research completed / Checking media / Completed); `publish` when
polling a /v1/publish request_id (then `result.posts[]` carries
per-platform post URLs).

status.description:
* `pending` — id issued, worker hasn't written the topic row yet
  (race window, usually <2s). The server caches issued ids in memory
  for 10 minutes so polling clients never see 404 during this window.
* `processing` — topic row exists, worker is on it. Stays in this
  state for the ENTIRE run (the abroll worker doesn't increment
  `step` until the final flip — don't expect granular progress).
* `completed` — scenes ready for review. (`result.review_url` is already populated from earlier states too — the completion signal is `stage` + `result.script`, not `review_url`.)
* `failed` — unrecoverable error (`error.code` + `error.message` populated).

stage.description: Fine-grained internal stage (informational, may evolve — don't gate logic on it).

progress.description:
Honest progress estimate (not step-based, since the worker stays at
step=0 for most of the run):
  * 0.05 — id issued, no topic row yet (pending / race)
  * 0.30 — topic row exists, no rendered script yet (worker starting)
  * 0.80 — script with segments present, finalisation pending
  * 1.00 — completed

skill_hint.description:
Informational nudge present on the `POST /v1/create_video` response
(NOT on `/v1/status` polls) when the supplied `script_text` looks
like the caller skipped `widecast_get_writing_skill` — e.g. no
inline `![alt](url)` markdown and no raw image/video URLs anywhere
in the script. The render still proceeds (auto-B-roll fills the
gap); this just teaches the AI to fetch the writing method next
time. The method is vendor-neutral — applies to any LLM.
skill_hint.example: script_text contains no inline media URLs. WideCast's writing method recommends …

agent_note.description:
Short instruction for AI agents that keep a local dashboard library: how to record this
piece (pass `result.library_record` to `<bridge> tool content import --json`, or run
`<bridge> tool provider call --operation getStatus --path id=<id>`). Present on the
`create_video`, `export_video` and `create_content` responses, and on a `publish`-type
status once it is `completed` / `failed`. Generic, harmless to ignore.

progress_hint.description:
UX-friendly sub-stage label derived from elapsed time (NOT from real
worker state). Present only while `status == "processing"`. Polling
AIs should relay `progress_hint.label` to the user every poll to
keep the wait feeling alive. The label includes an ETA suffix in
English (e.g. "Generating scene visuals · ~7 min left") — the AI is
expected to translate to the user's language. Pseudo-progress: the
stage may not exactly match what the worker is doing internally.

details.description:
Fine-grained worker state surfaced from the legacy topic / queue row.
`null` during the pending race window (no topic row yet). For abroll
(current pilot endpoint), most fields stay at default until the
worker flips to step=5+Completed at the end; the render pipeline
(future endpoint) will populate these progressively.

usage.description:
Cost & credit info. **`null` in pilot** — populated once billing
lands (ROADMAP Phase 1).

StatusResult.description:
Minimal user-facing output. The v0.1.0 pilot returns `review_url` for
every completed video (auth-adaptive: read-only embeddable player when
not signed in, full editor when signed in), and additionally `video_url`
when the video was created with `output_type: "video"` (or when
`/v1/export_video` finished). The rendered video script (with
segments) is intentionally NOT inlined to keep status responses cheap.
A future `GET /v1/videos/{id}/script` endpoint will serve the full
script explicitly when needed.

review_url.description:
URL where the end user views / edits the rendered scenes + audio.
Append **`&readonly=true`** to get a public, **read-only player**
(no sign-in) that does NOT block iframe embedding — use that variant
as an `<iframe>` src to show the result inline. The plain URL opens
the full editor for a signed-in user. Keyed by `topic_id`
(+ `company_id`). Default template:
`https://widecast.ai/#scene_editor?topic_id=<id>` (overridable
server-side via `WIDECAST_REVIEW_URL_TEMPLATE` env); embeddable
variant: `https://widecast.ai/#scene_editor?topic_id=<id>&readonly=true`.

video_url.description:
Direct URL to the rendered MP4. Populated only for videos created
with `output_type: "video"` or exported via `POST /v1/export_video`.

posts.description: Per-platform results. Present only on a `publish`-type status (`type == "publish"`).

post_url.description: Permalink; empty when the platform has none.

LibraryRecord.description:
A ready-to-file record of the piece for a local dashboard library — hand it to
`<bridge> tool content import --json` as is. Added next to `agent_note` on
`create_video`, `export_video`, `create_content`, `create_image` and (once final) a
`publish`-type status. Only the fields the server knows are filled; complete or
correct `title` / `body` with what you actually wrote or published.

status.description: `published` only when at least one platform succeeded; `draft` for everything else, including a failed publish.

script.description: Optional. The server never fills it (it does not echo your script back); add the narration script you sent when you record a create_video result.

urls.description:
`review` (viewer / editor), `public` (first live post or the first image), and one key per
platform that went live — `facebook`, or `facebook@2` for channel group 2.

ProgressHint.description:
Time-based pseudo-progress for UX during the 15-min create_video render
(and ~3-min export_video encode). Derived in the server from elapsed
time since the id was issued — NOT from real worker state — so the
stage label may not exactly match what the worker is doing internally.
Good enough for "show the user something" UX; not for gating logic.

Polling AIs should relay `label` to the user verbatim (translating to
the user's language as needed). `remaining_ms_estimate` is provided
separately for clients that want to format ETA differently than the
baked English "· ~N min left" suffix in `label`.

stage.description:
Machine-readable sub-stage key. Stable for code; not for display.
The set varies by what's running:
  * `create_video` `output_type=video` (full pipeline, ~15 min):
    queued / research / script / segmentation / voice_gen /
    image_gen / broll_fetch / composition / encoding / uploading
  * `create_video` `output_type=scene` (stops at scene editor, ~3 min):
    queued / research / script / segmentation / finalizing
  * `create_video` `output_type=text` (media-source Remake, ~3 min):
    queued / ingest / transcribe / script
  * `export_video` (post-review MP4 render, ~3 min):
    preparing / encoding_video / encoding_audio / muxing / uploading

label.description:
Human-readable English label with ETA suffix appended. Format:
`"<Sentence> · ~N min left"` (or `· Almost done` near the end).

elapsed_ms.description: Milliseconds since the id was issued.

remaining_ms_estimate.description:
Estimated milliseconds until completion (best-effort, ≥15 sec floor).
Drifts off if the worker is faster or slower than the typical timing.

ProcessingDetails.description:
Raw worker state for fine-grained progress visibility. Field names
mirror the legacy `topics_table` (or `video_queue_table`) schema.

⚠ **DELIBERATE NAME CLASH**: `details.status` is a free-form legacy
string ("Completed", "Error", "Avatar videos downloaded", …),
DISTINCT from the top-level `status` enum. Gate logic on the
top-level value; treat `details.status` as a human/debug hint.

step.description: Legacy `step` value (0 during abroll, 5 at completion). Render pipeline cycles 0→2→5.

status.description: Free-form legacy state string. NOT our top-level status enum.

notes.description: Free-form note from the worker (errors, assignment messages, etc.).

updated_at.description: When the worker last touched the row (ISO 8601 UTC).

input_truncated_from.description:
Original word count when the server auto-truncated a generative
input to its max (idea_text → 1000, blog_text → 3000). Only
present when the input exceeded the bound. Lets clients show
"your 4200-word article was trimmed to 3000 words" UX hints.

ListEnvelope.description:
**Pagination convention** for every future list endpoint.
Cursor-based — no list endpoint in v0.1.0 yet; this schema is reserved.

WebhookEvent.description:
The payload WideCast POSTs to your `callback_url`. Headers:
  * `User-Agent: WideCast-Webhook/<version>`
  * `X-WideCast-Event: <event_id>`
  * `X-WideCast-Event-Type: <event_type>`
  * `X-WideCast-Signature: t=<unix_ts>,v1=<hmac_sha256_hex>` — verify against `WIDECAST_WEBHOOK_SECRET`
  * `X-WideCast-Delivery: <uuid>` — unique per delivery attempt
  * `X-WideCast-Attempt: <n>` — 1-indexed retry counter

Retry: 10 attempts spread across 24h (offsets 0s/1m/5m/15m/30m/1h/3h/6h/12h/24h).
Acknowledge with HTTP 2xx within 30s; non-2xx triggers retry until
success, abandon (4xx), exhaustion (10 attempts), or 24h timeout.

event_id.description: Unique per event — dedupe on this in your handler.

event_type.description:
* `video.processing` — fires once, immediately after `POST /v1/create_video` (server has accepted, worker spawned).
* `video.completed` — fires once, when status first reaches `completed`. `data.result.review_url` populated.
* `video.failed` — fires once, when status first reaches `failed`. `data.error.{code,message}` populated.

details.description:
Code-specific structured data. Currently populated for
`code == "credit_exhausted"` and `code == "account_expired"`
(HTTP 402) — see `CreditErrorDetails`. Other error codes
leave this `null`.

CreditErrorDetails.description:
Structured upgrade / wait info attached to HTTP 402 responses
(`credit_exhausted` or `account_expired`). AI clients should surface
both options to the user — wait until the next monthly reset
(`reset_at`) OR upgrade now via `upgrade_url` — rather than only
relaying the prose `message`.

upgrade_url.description: Pricing page where the user can upgrade their plan.

reset_at.description:
ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when the user's current period ends and the
quota refreshes. Sourced from `system_configs.valid_to` — same
field that drives the `account_expired` gate (interpretation flips
based on whether `valid_to` is past or future relative to now).
Present for `credit_exhausted`; absent for `account_expired`.

expired_at.description:
ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when the paid plan expired.
Present for `account_expired`; absent for `credit_exhausted`.

renew_url.description:
Where the user renews an expired plan. Present for
`account_expired`; identical to `upgrade_url` in practice.

current_plan_quota.description: Monthly credit allocation on the user's current plan.

credits_remaining.description: Credits left in the user's current monthly allocation.

credits_required.description: Credits this operation would have consumed.

next_plan.description:
Suggested next plan to upgrade to (one tier above current).
`null` when the user is already on the top tier (Enterprise).

next_plan_quota.description: Monthly credit allocation on the suggested next plan.

SoloError.description: The shared error shape of the API (the same envelope as `Error`, produced by the server's `_wc_error`): `error.type` is `invalid_request_error` below HTTP 500 and `api_error` from 500. `error.code` says what was refused and `error.param` names the request field when there is one. A refusal can carry extra fields next to `code`, listed below.

opens_at.description: `outside_posting_hours` only: epoch seconds of the next time the posting hours open after the chosen instant.

tz.description: The zone the hours are in.

will_send.description: `audience_changed` of an email send: how many people would get it now.

will_post.description: `audience_changed` of a post send: how many groups would get it now.

expected.description: `csv_header` only: the columns the groups file must start with.

found.description: `csv_header` only: the columns the file started with.

SoloList.description: A list answer: `object` is `list` and `data` holds the items.

BroadcastEmail.description: One email of a client: its text, language, files and where it stands.

uid.description: The email's id, `bc_` followed by 26 characters.

client.description: The client slug.

body.description: The message text; `{{tag}}` and `{{tag|fallback}}` are filled per person.

language.description: `en` or `vi`: the language of the footer.

fallback.description: The word used for a `{{first_name}}` that is empty.

status.description: `draft` (the owner's), `awaiting_approval` (an agent's draft that waits for the owner), `sent` or `rejected`.

file_mode.description: How files go with the email: `none`, `link` or `attach`.

files.description: The files of the email in order.

file_key.description: The stored file's key, as returned by the file upload.

by_agent.description: True when an agent wrote the email.

last_run_id.description: The run id of the latest send of this email.

runs.description: How many times it was sent or scheduled.

stats.description: `email/get` only: the ledger counts of every send of this email (sent, delivered, bounced, complained, unsubscribed, opened, clicked...).

mail_list.description: `email/get` only: the email's uploaded mail list (`mode`, `columns`, `rows`, `count`, `file_name`).

updated_at.description: Epoch seconds of the last change.

BroadcastRun.description: One send of an email (a run): its state and its counts. A scheduled send has `state: scheduled` and the schedule fields.

run_id.description: The run id, `br_` followed by 26 characters.

planned.description: People the run was planned for. For a scheduled run: about how many people the audience held when it was scheduled; the audience is worked out again at send time.

skipped_optout.description: People skipped because they unsubscribed while the send ran.

held_for_tomorrow.description: People left for the next day because of the daily maximum.

done.description: The sum of sent, failed, unconfirmed and skipped.

pause_reason.description: Why the run paused or stopped, when it did.

transport.description: `ses` (the client's own sending link) or `sendbox` (Gmail sendboxes).

send_at.description: Scheduled runs: the time it goes out, epoch seconds.

send_at_tz.description: Scheduled runs: the zone the time is shown in.

via.description: `page` or `api`: where the send or the schedule came from.

expect_at_schedule.description: Scheduled runs: the count the caller expected when scheduling.

events.description: `run` and `history` only: the ledger counts of this run (delivered, bounced, complained, unsubscribed, opened, clicked...).

GroupPost.description: One post of a client: its text, versions, pictures and videos.

uid.description: The post's id, `gp_` followed by 26 characters.

body.description: The main text. `{{group_name}}` (or `{{group_name|word}}`) is filled per group.

language.description: `en` or `vi`: the language of the main text.

versions.description: Texts in the other language, by language code.

runs.description: How many times it was sent or scheduled.

stats.description: `post/get` only: where the post stands in every group (`counts` by state and one entry per group).

run.description: `post/get` only: the latest send of this post, or null.

GroupPostRun.description: One send of a post (a run). A run whose first copy is not due yet shows `state: scheduled`.

run_id.description: The run id, `gr_` followed by 26 characters.

state.description: `scheduled` (before the first copy is due), `running`, `paused`, `done` or `stopped`.

groups.description: Groups that got a copy in the plan.

send_at.description: Scheduled runs: when the first copy is due, epoch seconds.

send_at_tz.description: Scheduled runs: the zone the time is shown in.

Community.description: One community: the owner's own Facebook group fed every day.

id.description: The community id, `cm_` followed by 26 characters.

include.description: What a source post must be about.

exclude.description: What a source post must not be about.

sources.description: The groups the community reads, each with its read mark.

destinations.description: The groups it posts to, each with `waiting`, `queued`, `posted` and `buffer_days`.

waiting.description: Drafts that wait for the owner.

drafts.description: `get` only: the drafts that wait and the approved posts of the last 30 days and ahead.

CommunityDraft.description: One draft of a community post.

id.description: The draft id, `cd_` followed by 26 characters.

post_url.description: The link of the post once it is posted.

due_at.description: Epoch seconds the post goes out (approved drafts).

tz.description: The account owner's IANA time zone (UTC when it cannot be read).

tz_source.description: Where the zone came from: `default` when no zone was ever reported for the account, otherwise the place that reported it.

local_now.description: The current time in `tz`, ISO 8601 with the offset.

posting_hours.description: The hours Facebook posts may go out.

always.description: True when posting is allowed at any time.

open.description: True when the hours are open now; null when they cannot be read.

opens_at.description: Epoch seconds of the next opening, when closed.

closes_at.description: Epoch seconds of the next closing, when open.

min_ahead_s.description: The soonest a `send_at` may be, in seconds from now: 60.

max_ahead_days.description: The furthest a `send_at` may be, in days from now: 180.

SendsRow.description: One send or scheduled send in the history list.

id.description: The run id (email, post) or the copy id (community).

title.description: The email subject, or the first line of the post.

at.description: The scheduled time of an upcoming row; when it went out (or started) for a past row. Epoch seconds.

tz.description: The zone to show the time in.

next_at.description: When the next step happens, or null.

actions.description: What can still be done with it: the actions of the matching `schedule` operation.

link.description: The page path of this item.

children.description: A post send's copies, one per group.

Sendbox.description: One Gmail sendbox of the account. The app password is never returned.

last4.description: The last 4 characters of the stored password.

cap_today.description: How many emails the box may send today.

ceiling.description: The most a box of this kind may send a day.

daily_cap.description: The owner's own daily number, or null for the warm-up ramp.

broadcast_room.description: How many broadcast copies it can still send today.

GroupPostGroup.description: One Facebook group on a client's list.

key.description: The group's key: its number, or its name from the link, lower case.

member.description: `yes` when the posting account is a member, `no`, or empty when not checked yet.

removed.description: True when taken off the list.

daily_max.description: Most posts a day for the account, 1-20. Default 3 (the plan can cap it lower).

gap_min.description: Shortest gap between two posts in minutes, 5-720. Default 30.

group_cap_days.description: Window for the per-group limit, in days, 1-90. Default 7.

group_cap_max.description: Most posts one group gets in that window, 1-20. Default 1.

test_group_url.description: The group a test copy goes to.

last_send.description: What the last send was ticked with.

Unauthorized.description:
Missing, malformed, or revoked API key. Send a valid key as
`Authorization: Bearer wc_live_...`. `error.code` is `missing_api_key`
(no key) or `invalid_api_key` (malformed / unknown / revoked);
`error.type` is `authentication_error`.

PaymentRequired.description:
The account cannot be charged for this operation — `error.code` is
`credit_exhausted` (out of credits), `account_expired`,
`free_tier_limit_exceeded` (a Free account's script is over the Free
cap — `error.details.free_tier_max_words`) or `plan_required` (a
feature the account's plan does not include, e.g. `presenter` on a
Free / Trial account — `error.details.feature`). The
response carries an `error.details` object (see `CreditErrorDetails`)
with the upgrade URL, next monthly reset, and current/next plan info
so AI clients can format a "wait vs upgrade" choice for the user
instead of just relaying the prose message.

PreconditionFailed.description:
The request is well-formed but the resource is not in the expected
state — e.g. trying to export a video whose scenes are not yet
ready (`error.code = "scenes_not_ready"`).
